searches.label: Digital pathology, all tumor types (monitored journals)
Breast cancer + focus areas (all of PubMed, KI-JL 1–3)

articles.title: Time to maximal response of trastuzumab deruxtecan in patients with HER2-Positive metastatic breast cancer: A multicenter retrospective study (TRACE).
articles.why_relevant: A retrospective real-world study of T-DXd response kinetics in HER2-positive MBC with no biomarker, pathology, or resistance-mechanism analysis, so it only touches the group's anti-HER2 therapy interest.

articles.title: Computed tomography derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in high-risk breast cancer using fully automated deep learning algorithms.
articles.why_relevant: This is a small (n=127) CT-based deep learning study of body composition and cardiometabolic markers in breast cancer, with no histopathology, tumor biology, heterogeneity, or treatment-response angle, so it only touches the group's AI interest.

articles.title: Rechallenge, switch, or target? navigating advanced breast cancer after adjuvant CDK 4/6 inhibitors.
articles.why_relevant: A narrative review on resistance after adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors, covering biomarker-directed therapy, reassessment of tumor phenotype and longitudinal molecular profiling. It touches the group's interest in endocrine and CDK4/6i resistance and disease evolution, but it presents no original data, pathology or model component.

articles.title: Circulating miR-125b-5p and miR-210-3p are reduced in long-term breast cancer survivors with cardiovascular disease.
articles.why_relevant: This small exploratory study (n=24) examines circulating miRNAs as cardiovascular risk markers in breast cancer survivors, which lies outside the group's focus on tumor pathology, heterogeneity, resistance and patient-derived models.

articles.title: Association between screen-detected health-related social needs and nonadherence to endocrine therapy in patients with nonmetastatic breast cancer: an observational study.
articles.why_relevant: This EHR-based observational study links social needs to endocrine therapy nonadherence, with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, or model component, so it is only marginally related to the group's focus on tumor biology and resistance mechanisms.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Systematic analysis of metastasis-associated genes identifies miR-17-5p as a metastatic suppressor of basal-like breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This is a retraction note with no abstract or data; it only touches metastasis-associated gene biology in basal-like breast cancer and offers nothing the group can use directly, though it is a caution against relying on the retracted findings.

articles.title: Survival benefit of adding carboplatin to standard anthracycline-taxane chemotherapy in triple-negative breast cancer: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.why_relevant: A meta-analysis of randomized trials on adding carboplatin in TNBC chemotherapy with pCR and survival outcomes, but it has no biomarker, pathology, heterogeneity or model component and does not address predictors of response or resistance mechanisms.

articles.title: Response to Mokbel and Mokbel: SHBG and breast cancer risk in premenopausal women.
articles.why_relevant: A short author response to a letter on SHBG and breast cancer risk in premenopausal women, with no abstract and no pathology, biomarker-based treatment prediction, heterogeneity or model content relevant to the group.

articles.title: Cross-ancestry proteome-wide mendelian randomization of plasma proteins and breast cancer susceptibility.
articles.why_relevant: A germline-genetics and plasma proteomics Mendelian randomization study of breast cancer susceptibility; it is well validated across ancestries, but it addresses risk rather than tumor pathology, heterogeneity, treatment response or patient-derived models, so it has little overlap with the group's focus.

articles.title: Modeling the Effects of Clinical Breast Examination: Estimating Benefits and Harms From 2 Indian RCTs.
articles.why_relevant: A microsimulation of clinical breast examination screening in Indian RCTs is a screening and epidemiology study with no pathology, biomarker, AI, heterogeneity or patient-derived model component, so it is only marginally related to the group's research.

articles.title: Identifying Predictive Biomarkers of Resistance in Patients With Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Uses pretreatment transcriptomics from the large I-SPY2 trial to build and validate predictors of neoadjuvant resistance (RCBIII) across treatment arms and receptor subtypes, matching the group's focus on treatment prediction beyond routine IHC markers. Validation in non-overlapping I-SPY2 cohorts and a public exploration tool add value, though it is transcriptomic only, with no pathology or model-system component.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Response-weighted elastic net applied to pretreatment transcriptomes identified treatment-arm- and subtype-specific gene sets associated with resistance (RCBIII) to neoadjuvant therapy, implicating immune evasion, chromatin remodeling, DNA repair deficiency and HER2 signaling, and random forest models built on these gene sets predicted resistance in validation cohorts with moderate performance (sensitivity 0.61-0.88, specificity 0.65-0.74).
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Retrospective analysis of pretreatment transcriptomic data from 987 stage II-III breast cancer patients in the I-SPY2 trial for discovery across nine treatment arms and receptor subtypes, with validation in 1,127 non-overlapping I-SPY2 patients (independent paclitaxel control arms, paclitaxel plus immunotherapy arms, subtype-matched subsets), benchmarked against random gene sets, plus release of the public ISPY_Explore tool.
deep_analysis.limitation: Validation was performed only within the I-SPY2 trial (no external cohort), and the models showed modest specificity, with sensitivity and specificity trading off across arms, so generalizability beyond this trial is untested.

articles.title: Eosinophils in Breast Cancer: One for All and All for One.
articles.why_relevant: The title suggests a short editorial or comment on eosinophils in breast cancer (probably tumor microenvironment or immune biomarker related), but with no abstract or data it only touches the group's interests in biomarkers and tumor biology and offers little actionable content.

articles.title: Olanzapine or prochlorperazine added to antiemetic therapy for persistent chemotherapy-induced nausea: an NCORP phase 3 RCT.
articles.why_relevant: A supportive-care phase 3 RCT on antiemetics for chemotherapy-induced nausea in breast cancer patients, with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or model component relevant to the group's research.

articles.title: Validation of pathology-based triage for the 21-gene recurrence score: a meta-analysis and qualitative synthesis of the Magee equations.
articles.why_relevant: This meta-analysis of 13 studies (N=5396) validates routine-pathology-based triage (Magee equations using grade, ER/PR/HER2 and Ki67) as a way to predict Oncotype DX recurrence score, directly addressing risk assessment beyond routine IHC and the inter-observer variability in Ki67 and mitotic counting that AI pathology could standardize, although it contains no new AI or molecular data itself.

deep_analysis.central_finding: In a meta-analysis of 13 studies, Magee Equation scores below 18, calculated from routine pathology (grade, ER/PR/HER2, Ki-67), ruled out an Oncotype DX recurrence score of 26 or higher with a pooled NPV of 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.97) while sparing 62% of tests, and NPV rose to 0.99 at the RS 31 or higher threshold.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Systematic meta-analysis of 13 studies (N = 5396) in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer comparing Magee Equation outputs with Oncotype DX recurrence score, supplemented by a qualitative synthesis of discordance drivers.
deep_analysis.limitation: The Magee Equations depend on manually assessed inputs (mitotic counts and Ki-67 scoring) that show inter-observer variability, which the qualitative synthesis identifies as the main driver of discordance, and no AI or digital pathology data were evaluated, so the AI standardization benefit is only proposed.

articles.title: Real-world use of pembrolizumab in early-stage triple-negative breast cancer: Data from the French Early Access Program.
articles.why_relevant: A large real-world descriptive cohort of perioperative pembrolizumab in TNBC (pCR, safety, quality of life) with no biomarker, pathology or heterogeneity component, so it only touches the group's interest in treatment response and immunotherapy.

articles.title: Risk factors for early-onset cancers: Results from the JANUS cohort in Norway.
articles.why_relevant: A population-based epidemiology study of lifestyle and clinical risk factors for early-onset cancers (including breast cancer) with no pathology, biomarker, AI, heterogeneity or tumor-model component, so it only marginally touches the group's research.

articles.title: Second Cancer Risk in Female Survivors of Hodgkin Lymphoma: A National Cohort Analysis Across Treatment Eras.
articles.why_relevant: A population-based epidemiology study of second cancer risk (including breast cancer) in Hodgkin lymphoma survivors, with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or model component relevant to the group's research.

articles.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment.
articles.why_relevant: A large single-cell (855k cells, 159 patients) and spatial transcriptomics atlas of ER+ DCIS, normal breast and invasive cancer that maps microenvironment remodeling during progression, directly within the group's focus on intratumoral and spatial heterogeneity and a useful reference for spatial and morphology-linked analyses.

deep_analysis.central_finding: A single-cell and spatial atlas of estrogen-receptor positive DCIS, normal breast and invasive breast cancer identifies 9 cell types and 60 cell states and shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular cells and basal cells around DCIS regions, along with immunosuppressive ducts that support preinvasive cancer cell growth, with many changes persisting into invasive disease.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Fresh samples from normal breast tissue, ER+ DCIS and invasive breast cancer were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing (854,911 cells from 159 patients) and spatial transcriptomics (39 samples).
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract does not describe independent validation cohorts or longitudinal outcome data, and the cross-sectional sampling is restricted to ER+ disease, so inferences about progression from DCIS to invasive cancer rest on comparing different patients' samples rather than tracking the same lesions over time.

articles.title: Late Recurrence After Radiotherapy Omission in Younger Postmenopausal Patients With Breast Cancer: The IDEA Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
articles.why_relevant: The IDEA trial is a nonrandomized study of radiotherapy omission guided by the Oncotype DX recurrence score, so it has a peripheral biomarker link, but no abstract is available and it is mainly a clinical outcomes study with no digital pathology, heterogeneity or model component.

articles.title: Patterns of metastasis according to germline BRCA1/2 mutation status in patients with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This retrospective study of 184 patients links germline BRCA1/2 status to metastatic site patterns within HR+ and TNBC, which is adjacent to the group's interest in metastatic biology and tumor-metastasis heterogeneity, but it is a small single-cohort clinical analysis with no pathology, imaging-AI or molecular mechanism component.

articles.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis.
articles.why_relevant: A Nature study of single-cell epigenetic profiling of treatment-naive luminal breast tumours that finds a recurrent basal-like subpopulation with reduced hormone receptor signalling, and links a blood-based epigenetic signature to relapse risk. This bears directly on the group's interest in intratumoral heterogeneity, biology beyond routine ER/PR IHC, and endocrine resistance.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Single-cell epigenetic profiling of treatment-naive luminal breast tumours identifies a recurrent basal-like cell subpopulation with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients, marked by aggressive oncogenic traits, reduced hormone receptor signalling and altered H3K4 mono- and trimethylation, and a related basal epigenetic signature measured on cell-free nucleosomes in blood is associated with early diagnosis and with relapse risk.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Epigenetic CyTOF (mass cytometry) of freshly resected treatment-naive human luminal tumours, compared with whole-genome DNA methylation deconvolution and single-cell proteomic versus genomic profiling of H3K4me1/me3, plus single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood plasma for diagnosis and prognosis.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract does not report cohort sizes or independent validation, and the findings rest on bulk-derived deconvolution and a targeted marker panel, so the cohort scale and generalisability of the blood-based diagnostic and prognostic signature are unclear.

articles.title: Hypermethylation in CpG-rich cfDNA fragments enables accurate detection of circulating tumor DNA in BRCA1- and BRCA2-associated breast and ovarian cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A small pilot cfDNA methylation ctDNA assay (31 breast cancers, panel derived from TCGA/GEO, modest sensitivity of 38.7% in breast cancer) in BRCA1/2 carriers; it is only tangentially related to the group's tissue-based pathology, heterogeneity and resistance focus.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided deep learning framework with whole slide images for molecular subtyping of breast cancer: a multicentre, retrospective study.
articles.why_relevant: A multicentre cross-modal study (n=1283) using IHC whole-slide images (HER2, ER, PR, Ki-67) to guide ultrasound-based molecular subtyping, which touches on biopsy–surgical IHC discordance and heterogeneity, but at inference it is an ultrasound-only tool, so it is adjacent to the group's H&E/WSI pathology AI work rather than a direct contribution.

articles.title: Temporal control of CAR expression by a tumor-targeting albumin adapter and logic gating enhances CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumors.
articles.why_relevant: This is a preclinical engineering study of synNotch-gated CAR-T cells, with breast cancer used only as one in vivo model, and it has no connection to pathology, biomarkers, heterogeneity or patient-derived models.

articles.title: Impact of multidisciplinary tumor meetings on clinical outcomes, treatment concordance, and guideline adherence in breast cancer: a systematic review with emphasis on older patients.
articles.why_relevant: A systematic review of multidisciplinary tumor meetings and guideline adherence in older breast cancer patients, with no pathology, biomarker, AI, heterogeneity or patient-derived model component, so it is only marginally relevant to the group's research.

articles.title: Palbociclib, Fulvestrant, Trastuzumab, and Pyrotinib for Patients with Advanced Breast Cancer with Brain Metastases: A Prospective Multicenter Phase 2 Trial.
articles.why_relevant: A small single-arm phase 2 trial of CDK4/6 inhibitor, endocrine and anti-HER2 combination therapy in HR+/HER2+ breast cancer with brain metastases; it touches on the group's interest in endocrine and anti-HER2 therapy, but it has no biomarker, pathology or resistance-mechanism analysis.

articles.title: CD39-associated myeloid-T-cell coordination within an immunoregulatory neighborhood linked to treatment resistance in triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Combines scRNA-seq re-analysis, CosMx spatial transcriptomics, multiplex IF and an independent 112-patient IHC cohort to link CD39-associated myeloid/T-cell neighborhoods to anti-PD-L1 plus chemotherapy resistance in TNBC, which touches on spatial heterogeneity and resistance mechanisms but is immunology-focused with a small cohort and little overlap with the group's AI pathology or patient-derived model work.

articles.title: Breast density and risk factors for interval and screen-detected breast cancers: a case-case analysis of the Breast Cancer Now Generations Study, UK.
articles.why_relevant: A well-conducted epidemiological case-case study of breast density and risk factors for interval versus screen-detected cancers, but it has no pathology, AI, molecular or tumor-biology component, so it is only tangentially related to the group's focus on precision pathology and treatment prediction.

articles.title: Molecular and clinical predictors of NAC response and relapse in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: It addresses prediction of neoadjuvant chemotherapy response and relapse in HR+/HER2- breast cancer beyond routine IHC, with matched primary, residual and metastatic transcriptomics relevant to resistance and heterogeneity. However, the cohort is very small (n=44), validation is limited, and there is no pathology or AI component, which limits its value to the group.

articles.title: Bacterial lipopolysaccharide mediates the interplay between tumor microbiome and immune microenvironment in breast cancer: development of a prognostic risk score.
articles.why_relevant: This is mainly a public-database (CTD/TCGA/GEO) prognostic gene signature with a small 56-patient validation cohort and a 4T1 mouse experiment; the tumor microbiome and immune microenvironment link is only loosely adjacent to the group's focus on precision pathology, heterogeneity and resistance.

articles.title: Real-world patient experiences in HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer: a study of symptom and side effect reporting by patients and physicians.
articles.why_relevant: A cross-sectional survey of patient-physician symptom reporting and quality of life in HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or model component, so it falls outside the group's translational focus.

articles.title: Chemoendocrine therapy versus tamoxifen with ovarian function suppression in women with node-positive breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A retrospective, propensity-matched clinical comparison of adjuvant chemoendocrine therapy versus tamoxifen plus OFS in premenopausal ER+/HER2- node-positive breast cancer, with only routine clinicopathologic variables (PR, Ki-67, grade) and no new biomarker, AI or heterogeneity component, so it is of limited relevance to the group's focus.

articles.title: The landscape of cell surface target expression in treatment resistant early-stage breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Links cell-surface ADC and other targeted-therapy targets (e.g. EPCAM, CEACAM5, NECTIN4) to treatment resistance and recurrence across breast cancer subtypes, with single-cell evidence of intratumoral heterogeneity. It is primarily a retrospective mining of public and cohort transcriptomic data (SCAN-B, neoadjuvant aggregates, one randomized trial) with RNA-protein correlation but no experimental or tissue-level validation, so it is background reading and not a must-read.

articles.title: Pertuzumab in HER2-positive breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.why_relevant: A meta-analysis of pertuzumab RCTs in HER2-positive breast cancer that covers anti-HER2 therapy efficacy and safety, but it has no biomarker, pathology, heterogeneity or resistance-mechanism component and reports no new data, so it is only loosely related to the group's focus.

articles.title: Dose-dense neoadjuvant bi-weekly nab-paclitaxel followed by epirubicin-cyclophosphamide versus bi-weekly docetaxel followed by epirubicin-cyclophosphamide in patients with HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a multicentre, randomised, phase III trial.
articles.why_relevant: A phase III neoadjuvant chemotherapy trial in HR+/HER2- breast cancer that uses RCB and pCR as endpoints, but it has no biomarker, pathology-AI or heterogeneity component, so it is only tangentially related to the group's focus on treatment-response prediction.

articles.title: Decoding neutrophil spatial heterogeneity and clinical implications in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A Cancer Cell study that combines AI-based computational pathology on H&E (n=1,113) with single-cell spatial omics (n=104) to resolve neutrophil spatial heterogeneity in breast cancer, validates the findings experimentally, and shows prognostic and immunotherapy-predictive value beyond established biomarkers in TNBC. This falls squarely within the group's interests in spatial heterogeneity, AI pathology and treatment prediction.

deep_analysis.central_finding: In breast cancer, especially TNBC, neutrophil spatial patterns carry distinct clinical meaning: neutrophil–tumor cell proximity associated with favorable prognosis (via neutrophils enhancing tumor MHC I expression through inflammatory crosstalk), while neutrophil–immune cell proximity predicted better immunotherapy response and marked an antigen-presenting neutrophil phenotype that could be augmented by targeting polyamine metabolism.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: The study integrated AI-powered computational pathology on routine slides (n = 1,113) with single-cell spatial omics (n = 104) in large breast cancer cohorts, and supported the findings with experimental validation of the mechanisms.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract does not specify cohort composition, independent external validation, or the size of the immunotherapy-treated subset, so the generalizability of the spatial patterns as predictive biomarkers, particularly for immunotherapy response, cannot be judged.

articles.title: Neutrophils are known by their neighbors in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This Cancer Cell preview covers a study that combines large-scale computational pathology, spatial omics and functional experiments to define prognostic and immunotherapy-associated neutrophil niches in TNBC, which fits the group's interests in AI on H&E slides, spatial heterogeneity and treatment-response prediction. It is a short commentary rather than the primary study, so it is a pointer to the original paper (Xu et al.), which is the one to read.

deep_analysis.central_finding: This preview describes Xu et al., who identify two spatially defined neutrophil niches in triple-negative breast cancer with different clinical associations: tumor-proximal neutrophils are linked to favorable prognosis, whereas neutrophils near immune cells are associated with immunotherapy response.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: The article is a short Cancer Cell commentary on a primary study that combined large-scale computational pathology, spatial omics and functional experiments in triple-negative breast tumors; the abstract gives no cohort sizes or validation details.
deep_analysis.limitation: As a brief preview it reports only the headline findings, with no cohort numbers, validation data or mechanistic detail, so the strength of the evidence cannot be judged without the original Xu et al. paper.

articles.title: Cancer Risks Associated With Germline BARD1 Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic Variants: A Multicenter Study of 445 Families.
articles.why_relevant: A germline BARD1 pedigree and cancer-risk study with implications for genetic counselling, but it has no pathology, tumor-biology, heterogeneity, or treatment-response component, so it is only loosely adjacent to the group's focus on molecular profiling.

articles.title: Freezing-induced solid-liquid microphase separation for self-assembly of functional nucleic acid nanoparticles.
articles.why_relevant: This is a nanomaterials/nucleic acid delivery chemistry paper that only uses breast cancer cell lines as a demonstration, with no connection to pathology, biomarkers, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models.

articles.title: The deep learning framework Hist2Prot infers single-cell spatial proteomics from histology to predict biomarkers and clinical outcomes.
articles.why_relevant: A high-impact, well-validated deep learning method (about 51M training cells, 1,774 patients across seven cohorts) that infers single-cell spatial proteomics from routine H&E to predict biomarkers, prognosis and immunotherapy response, closely matching the group's focus on clinical-grade AI on H&E and on spatial heterogeneity beyond routine IHC, even though it is pan-cancer rather than breast-specific.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Hist2Prot, a deep learning framework, generates single-cell spatial proteomic profiles from routine H&E histology that match measured protein profiles, outperform established baselines, preserve immune, stromal and tumor cell phenotypes and tumor microenvironment organization, and improve prediction of molecular biomarkers, prognosis and immunotherapy response over H&E morphology alone.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: The model was trained on about 51 million paired cells from a same-section G4X spatial proteomics dataset and evaluated in internal test cohorts, independent same-platform G4X cohorts and external cross-platform datasets (about 72 million additional cells), with downstream clinical prediction tested across seven independent patient cohorts totalling 1,774 patients.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract does not state which tumor types, protein panels or clinical endpoints are covered, so it is unclear how far the training data (a single G4X platform) support generalisation, or whether the inferred virtual proteins reflect true protein expression rather than morphology-derived correlations, especially across platforms.

articles.title: AI-based prediction of actionable genomic alterations from H&E-stained slides.
articles.why_relevant: A perspective (not original data) on deep learning prediction of actionable genomic alterations from H&E slides, including prospective validation and clinical integration, which is conceptually close to the group's clinical-grade AI-on-H&E work, but it is not breast-specific and offers no new data or methods.

articles.title: Validation of DNA methylation subtype as a prognostic biomarker in pediatric adrenocortical tumors: re-evaluation of results from the COG ARAR0332 clinical trial.
articles.why_relevant: Validates a DNA methylation-based prognostic classifier in pediatric adrenocortical tumors, which is a methodologically sound molecular risk-stratification study. However, it is not about breast cancer, uses no digital pathology or AI on slides, and does not address heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models, so its relevance to the group is limited.

articles.title: Interpreting and Validating a Deep Learning Model Predictive of Spatial Morphologic-Molecular Patterns in Lung Adenocarcinoma, Using Ground Truth Immunohistochemistry Images.
articles.why_relevant: Although it concerns lung adenocarcinoma, it presents an explainable deep learning model that predicts spatial gene expression heterogeneity from H&E whole-slide images and validates it against ground-truth IHC in an external clinical cohort, which closely matches the group's work on AI-based morpho-molecular and heterogeneity analysis (the modest external cohort and AUCs of 0.64-0.92 temper enthusiasm).

deep_analysis.central_finding: XpressO-Lung, an explainable deep learning model trained on H&E diagnostic whole-slide images paired with bulk transcriptomics, predicted spatial expression patterns of ten genes (e.g., NAPSA, CD8A, TTF1, KRT7, TP53) in LUAD with AUCs of 0.64–0.92, and these patterns matched known tumor–microenvironment morphology and IHC-observed features.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Model development used 200 TCGA LUAD cases (H&E Dx-WSIs with bulk transcriptomic labels), with spatial validation by immunohistochemistry on an external set of clinical LUAD samples from Dartmouth Health.
deep_analysis.limitation: The model learns from bulk transcriptomic labels rather than spatially resolved ground truth, so spatial predictions are only indirectly validated, and the validation relies on a small external cohort and concordance with histomorphology; AUCs for some genes are modest (as low as 0.64).

articles.title: Multimodal Deep Learning Prognostic Model for Predicting Treatment Outcomes for Oropharyngeal Carcinoma.
articles.why_relevant: A multimodal deep learning prognostic model for oropharyngeal cancer built on CT and clinical data, not breast cancer and not histopathology; the gain over clinical-only is marginal (C-index 0.718 vs 0.705), and there is no external validation, so it offers only loose methodological parallels to the group's AI risk-prediction work.

articles.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A high-impact Nat Med study that uses supervised computational pathology to quantify subcellular TROP2 on IHC slides and predict ADC response, with validation in a phase 3 trial. It is directly transferable to the group's work on AI-based biomarker scoring beyond visual IHC, ADC response prediction and HER2-low-style quantification in breast cancer, even though the tumor type is NSCLC.

deep_analysis.central_finding: A supervised computational pathology score of TROP2 on IHC slides, the normalized membrane ratio (membrane relative to membrane plus cytoplasmic TROP2), identified nonsquamous NSCLC patients with longer progression-free survival on Dato-DXd (median 7.2 vs 4.0 months; HR 0.40) but not on docetaxel (HR 0.94), with a significant treatment-by-biomarker interaction (P = 0.0098).
deep_analysis.design_and_data: TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS) was developed to quantify TROP2 in individual tumor cells and subcellular compartments on IHC slides; NMR was derived in TROPION-PanTumor01 (n = 115 biomarker-evaluable advanced NSCLC), and its cut-point was optimized and validated in TROPION-Lung01 (n = 352 biomarker-evaluable, including n = 221 nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations) comparing Dato-DXd with docetaxel.
deep_analysis.limitation: The cut-point was optimized and validated within a single phase 3 trial (TROPION-Lung01) using retrospective biomarker-evaluable subsets, with the primary analysis restricted to nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable alterations, so independent external validation and generalizability are not shown.

articles.title: Comprehensive phenotyping of intratumoral fibrosis in gastric carcinomas with poorly differentiated histology: associations with clinicopathological features.
articles.why_relevant: It applies digital image analysis (FibroNest) to quantify stromal collagen architecture and links it to metastasis and recurrence, which touches on tumor microenvironment heterogeneity. However, it is a gastric cancer study with only 30 patients, no independent validation, and no breast cancer or AI/deep learning component, so its direct relevance is limited.

articles.title: The COSAS 2024 challenge: Cross-Organ and Cross-Scanner Adenocarcinoma Segmentation for domain generalization in computational pathology.
articles.why_relevant: A benchmark of domain generalization across organs and scanners, including foundation-model baselines, directly addresses the robustness needed for clinical-grade H&E AI tools, although it is not breast-specific and is limited to segmentation of adenocarcinoma patches.

deep_analysis.central_finding: In the COSAS 2024 challenge, adenocarcinoma segmentation performance varied substantially across organs and scanners and between the two tasks, with no model family (conventional or foundation-model baselines) uniformly best, while top submissions reached competitive results through different mixes of augmentation, multi-domain training, model design and inference-time refinement.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: A benchmark challenge with separate cross-organ and cross-scanner segmentation tasks, using 580 pixel-level annotated histopathology patches from six organ sites and six scanner platforms, 30 international teams submitting valid solutions (CNN, transformer and hybrid architectures), plus organizer-run conventional and foundation-model baselines.
deep_analysis.limitation: The benchmark is limited to patch-level adenocarcinoma segmentation (580 patches across six organs and scanners, not breast-specific), so conclusions about generalization may not extend to whole-slide, other tumor types, or clinical workflow settings.

articles.title: Foundation-model imaging biomarkers for pancreatic cancer: cross-species discovery of conserved tumour biology in mouse MRI and human CT.
articles.why_relevant: A foundation-model imaging biomarker study in pancreatic cancer using radiology (MRI/CT) rather than histopathology, so it is outside the group's breast and H&E focus; the main overlap is the methodological idea of frozen foundation-model embeddings linked to tumour biology (CD8, stroma), but there is no external validation and the data are CPTAC only.

articles.title: Digital pathology does not improve the prognostic performance of Ki-67 in a large cohort of penile cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Not breast cancer, but it directly addresses Ki-67 scoring by digital image analysis (HALO) versus pathologists, including interobserver variability and cut-off dependence, which is a methodological caution for the group's Ki-67 and AI-based scoring work; it is a modest single-cohort retrospective study in a rare tumor type.

articles.title: Targeting AP1S1 modulates the unfolded protein response and cell cycle and sensitizes triple-negative breast cancer to erlotinib.
articles.why_relevant: It links a candidate gene (AP1S1) to intrinsic TKI resistance in TNBC using cell lines, patient-derived organoids and scRNA-seq, which touches the group's interests in resistance mechanisms and patient-derived models. However, it is a single-gene functional study with public-database mining, modest validation in patient material, and a level-1 journal.

articles.title: Phytochemical-rich fraction from raw and cooked kodo millet (Paspalum scrobiculatum L.) reduced the viability of colorectal- and breast cancer cells in vitro by inducing apoptosis.
articles.why_relevant: A food-science study of millet extract cytotoxicity in MDA-MB-231 and colorectal cell lines; it has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived model component, so it only touches breast cancer cell lines.

articles.title: Targeting the SND1-MTDH/FANCD2 axis impairs DNA repair and sensitizes triple-negative breast cancer to PARP inhibitor.
articles.why_relevant: A TNBC mechanism study of DNA repair and PARP inhibitor sensitization with a peptide inhibitor tested in patient-derived organoids and xenografts, which touches the group's resistance and patient-derived model interests. It is a preclinical, drug-development paper with no pathology, heterogeneity or biomarker-validation component in patient cohorts.

articles.title: PARP inhibitors in breast cancer: From DNA repair targeting to next-generation precision therapeutics.
articles.why_relevant: A review of PARPi resistance mechanisms (BRCA reversion, HR restoration, ctDNA clonal evolution) and predictive biomarkers (RAD51 foci, computational and imaging approaches) that touches the group's resistance and biomarker themes. It reports no new primary data and has limited direct link to digital pathology, so it is useful background to skim.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Disease-Free Survival in Breast Cancer Incorporating Clinical and Treatment Information: Retrospective Cohort Study With External Validation.
articles.why_relevant: Tabular clinicopathological ML prognostic model (XGBoost) for breast cancer DFS with TCGA external validation, with no image, molecular or patient-derived model component, so it is only loosely related to the group's focus on risk assessment beyond routine biomarkers.

articles.title: Pyramid-level training with stain normalization for breast cancer lymph-node metastasis segmentation in whole-slide images.
articles.why_relevant: A WSI deep-learning segmentation study in breast cancer, but it is an incremental training and sampling pipeline on the CAMELYON benchmark for lymph-node metastasis detection, with weak external validation (Dice 70.6% on BCSS) and no link to biomarkers, heterogeneity or treatment prediction.

articles.title: KLRB1 (CD161) as a context-dependent prognostic marker in breast cancer: An exploratory analysis of CD4+ memory T cell infiltration: a retrospective multi-cohort study.
mesh_terms: NK Cell Lectin-Like Receptor Subfamily B*
articles.why_relevant: It is an exploratory prognostic-marker study that mainly mines TCGA/METABRIC with xCell deconvolution, adding only small single-cell (n=3), Xenium (19 samples) and a single-pair mIF dataset. The spatial and immune-microenvironment angle touches on heterogeneity, but the validation is weak, the findings are inconsistent after full adjustment, and the authors state it does not support clinical use.

articles.title: Cell-Cell Communication Network Analysis of Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of TLS in TNBC versus ER+ breast cancer touches on spatial heterogeneity, but it relies only on public datasets (7 TNBC and 12 ER+ TLS) with no functional or independent patient validation, so its value to the group is limited.

articles.title: Impact of post-thaw incubation time on viability and neovascularization of cryopreserved human ovarian tissue.
articles.why_relevant: This is a fertility-preservation study of cryopreserved human ovarian cortex, with a CAM graft model, and it is not about breast cancer biology, pathology, or tumor models, so it only touches the group's areas through Ki-67 IHC and an ex vivo tissue culture setup.

articles.title: SIMMPYRA1 and SIMMPYRA2 suppress triple-negative breast cancer growth through selective STAT3 inhibition.
articles.why_relevant: A preclinical drug-discovery study of STAT3 inhibitors in TNBC that uses PDX models for in vivo efficacy, but it lacks a pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity or resistance-mechanism angle, so it only touches the group's patient-derived model interest.

articles.title: Population-scale integration of spatial omics networks for clinical prediction and biological discovery by SPIN.
articles.why_relevant: A spatial single-cell network framework for population-level outcome prediction, tested on a breast cancer proteomics cohort (C-index 0.78) alongside an Alzheimer's cohort; it is methodologically adjacent to the group's spatial heterogeneity and risk-prediction work, but it is not breast-specific, is not H&E-based, and shows limited independent validation.

articles.title: Benchmarking cell segmentation in two Spatialomics platforms with open-source software.
articles.why_relevant: Benchmarks 14 cell segmentation methods on spatial proteomics images of melanoma and breast cancer against pathologist ground truth, which is useful methodological background for spatial and heterogeneity work, though it does not use H&E or clinical-grade AI and has no clinical validation.

articles.title: Peritoneal carcinomatosis and bowel obstruction as an unusual presentation of metastatic breast carcinoma.
articles.why_relevant: A single case report of ER-positive to ER-negative receptor discordance in a peritoneal metastasis touches on primary-metastasis heterogeneity, but it is anecdotal and offers no mechanistic, cohort or methodological insight.

articles.title: Advances in gold and silver nanoplatforms for photon therapies in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A review of gold and silver nanoparticle platforms for photothermal, photodynamic and radiotherapy in breast cancer; it touches heterogeneity and resistance only in passing and has no pathology, biomarker, AI or patient-derived model component relevant to the group.

articles.title: Deep learning-based enhancing spatial biological context parsing.
articles.why_relevant: CroSP is a multimodal graph-autoencoder method that combines spatial transcriptomics with histology images for spatial domain identification, including a breast cancer heterogeneity and immune microenvironment analysis, which is adjacent to the group's spatial heterogeneity and image-omics interests. It is mainly a methods paper benchmarked on public datasets (brain, olfactory bulb) with limited breast cancer validation or clinical translation.

articles.title: Subtype-resolved tumor-intrinsic programs in immune-cold breast cancer: mechanistic interactions, evidence gaps, and translational priorities.
articles.why_relevant: A narrative review of tumor-intrinsic immune-cold mechanisms and ICB resistance by breast cancer subtype, with a biomarker-matching angle, but it presents no original data and is only adjacent to the group's focus on pathology, AI and patient-derived models.

articles.title: Network pharmacology and machine learning nominate PPARG as a candidates target of Aegle marmelos (L.) Correa phytochemicals in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A purely in silico network pharmacology, docking and machine-learning study of plant phytochemicals, trained on a single public dataset (GSE42568) with no experimental or patient-material validation, so it has essentially no connection to the group's work on digital pathology, tumor heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models.

articles.title: Determination of drug sensitivity in patient derived models of breast cancer by multiparametric quantitative phase imaging.
articles.why_relevant: Presents a rapid, label-free single-cell functional drug-sensitivity assay applied to breast cancer PDX organoids and cryopreserved primary patient samples, quantifying intrapatient heterogeneity and acquired resistance, which fits the group's patient-derived model, ex vivo testing and drug-response heterogeneity work, though the sample set is small and the journal is level 1.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Multiparametric quantitative phase imaging (mQPI) detected drug-response differences and heterogeneous response dynamics at single-cell level in patient-derived breast cancer models without labeling, including distinct profiles between cells from different anatomical sites of the same patient and in acquired-resistance models.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: mQPI was applied to cells from patient-derived xenograft organoid (PDXO) models, including models of acquired resistance and multi-site samples from one patient, and to viably cryopreserved primary breast cancer samples tested either directly after thawing or after 2 weeks of short-term expansion.
deep_analysis.limitation: The sample set is small (a few PDXO models and a few cryopreserved primary samples), with no clinical outcome correlation or benchmarking against other functional assays reported in the abstract, so predictive value for patient response remains untested.

articles.title: Analyzing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC): an integrative transcriptomic and computational study.
articles.why_relevant: A computational network-toxicology study that mines public TNBC transcriptomic data for a PFAS-linked prognostic signature, with no measured PFAS exposure and only small RT-qPCR validation (15 paired samples); it has little connection to the group's pathology, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived model work.

articles.title: KCNQ3 as a pan-cancer prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target: Multi-omics profiling and mechanistic validation in cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.why_relevant: A pan-cancer public-database analysis of KCNQ3 with mechanistic validation in cholangiocarcinoma only; breast cancer is mentioned only as one of many tumor types, and the work has no pathology, heterogeneity-in-patient-material or breast-specific angle.

articles.title: Mechanotransduction in breast cancer and implications for preclinical modeling.
articles.why_relevant: A review of mechanotransduction in breast cancer and how well preclinical models (organoids, 3D cultures, organ-on-chip, animal models) reproduce it, with a model validation framework that is useful background for the group's patient-derived model work, although it presents no primary data or patient-material validation.

articles.title: CD97 Modulates M1-Like Macrophage Activation and Function to Influence the Immune Microenvironment and Tumor Progression in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This TNBC study of CD97 in macrophages relies mainly on public datasets (TCGA, KM Plotter, GEO) and THP-1 cell line models, with no patient-material validation and an inconsistent prognostic signal. It is only loosely connected to the group's work on tumor microenvironment and heterogeneity.

articles.title: Subtype conversion and metastatic timing in breast cancer liver metastasis.
articles.why_relevant: Directly addresses primary-metastasis subtype discordance (42.9% conversion in 205 paired breast cancer liver metastases) and its link to metastatic timing, which fits the group's heterogeneity theme, but it is a retrospective clinical-pathological analysis with no molecular, AI or mechanistic depth, published in a level 1 journal.

articles.title: Dynamic changes in ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67, and AR before and after neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer and their clinicopathological significance: a single-center real-world study.
articles.why_relevant: This large (n=644) retrospective study of ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67 and AR conversion after neoadjuvant therapy touches the group's interests in receptor discordance, HER2 loss and treatment response beyond routine IHC. However, it is single-centre and descriptive, offers no mechanistic, spatial or AI component, and was published in a level 1 journal, so it is background reading rather than a priority.

articles.title: Organoid-Guided Precision Salvage Therapy for Advanced Breast Cancer with Multiple Metastases: A Case Report.
articles.why_relevant: It touches on the group's patient-derived organoid and functional drug testing area, with PDOs from a liver metastasis guiding salvage therapy, but as a single uncontrolled case report it cannot show predictive accuracy and has little methodological or validation value.

articles.title: Use of prepectoral polyurethane coated implants in the setting of radiotherapy: the OPBC-09 PRExRT retrospective cohort study.
articles.why_relevant: This retrospective surgical cohort study compares implant types for breast reconstruction after radiotherapy and has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or model component relevant to the group's research.

articles.title: Incidence and mortality of breast cancer among adolescent and young adult women worldwide in 2022 and projections for 2040: Implications for surgery.
articles.why_relevant: A GLOBOCAN-based epidemiological burden and projection study of AYA breast cancer with surgical-capacity implications, with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity or model component relevant to the group.

articles.title: Toward Improved Methodology to Measure the Uptake of Mammography in Populations Using Insurance Claims: A Case Study From Delaware, USA.
articles.why_relevant: A population-level epidemiology and health-services methods study on mammography uptake from insurance claims, with no pathology, biomarker, AI, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived model component relevant to the group.

articles.title: An outer membrane vesicle-associated two-track model for enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis oncogenesis.
articles.why_relevant: This is a hypothesis/review-style paper on ETBF oncogenesis, mainly colonic, with only a peripheral link to breast cancer (a GAK-NUMB-NOTCH1-HEY1 axis tied to cancer stem cells and chemoresistance in breast cancer cells), and it has no pathology, AI, heterogeneity or patient-derived model component for the group.

articles.title: A shapley additive exPlanations (SHAP)-driven quantitative ultrasound radiomics model for non-invasive HER2 status prediction in invasive breast cancer based on intratumoral and peritumoral habitat features.
articles.why_relevant: It predicts HER2 status, including IHC 0 vs 1+ (HER2-low), from ultrasound radiomics, which touches the group's HER2 biomarker interest, but it is imaging rather than histopathology. Performance is modest (AUC about 0.67-0.79), the design is retrospective and single-center, and there is no external validation.

articles.title: Stromal VEGF-C expression predicts nodal metastasis: implications for axillary surgery de-escalation in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A prospective-cohort IHC biomarker study (stromal VEGF-C) with an automated image-analysis script separating stromal from epithelial cells to predict nodal metastasis, which touches on risk assessment beyond routine markers and digital image analysis. However, it is a single-cohort observational study without independent validation, and the image analysis is a simple script rather than a deep learning method.

articles.title: High-throughput spatial proteomics from cellular to subcellular scales via a hanging droplet workflow.
articles.why_relevant: A high-throughput FFPE laser-microdissection spatial proteomics workflow reaching near single-cell depth, demonstrated on breast cancer subtypes and microenvironments, which is a usable method for studying intratumoral spatial heterogeneity and linking H&E-guided regions to protein-level biomarkers (HER2, PR, TP53), though the breast cancer application is a proof of concept.

deep_analysis.central_finding: A 96-well hanging-droplet micro-FFPE workflow combining whole-slide imaging, laser microdissection and narrow-window DIA mass spectrometry takes tissue lysis to LC-MS-ready peptides on Evotips in ~2 hours, quantifies >5,500 protein groups from ~250 cells (50,000 µm²) and ~2,500 from ~5 cells (1,000 µm²), and resolves breast cancer subtypes and microenvironments via TP53, HER2 and PR.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Methods-development study on FFPE tissue that benchmarks the protocol against reference methods (~30% shorter preparation, up to 192 samples in parallel) across microdissected region sizes from ~250 cells down to ~5 cells and ~60 µm² single-nucleus regions (~1,800 protein groups), with a breast cancer FFPE application for subtype and microenvironment profiling; the abstract does not state the cohort size.
deep_analysis.limitation: The breast cancer application appears to be a proof of concept; the abstract does not report cohort size or independent validation, so it is unclear whether subtype and microenvironment resolution holds across patients or intratumoral heterogeneity.

articles.title: Activity and safety of first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial.
articles.why_relevant: A single-arm phase 1b/2 trial of a PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody plus nab-paclitaxel in TNBC with no biomarker, pathology or heterogeneity analysis, so it is only tangentially related to the group's focus despite the high-impact journal.

articles.title: Co-targeting angiogenesis and immune checkpoints in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: No abstract is available and the title suggests a short comment or commentary on angiogenesis and immune-checkpoint co-targeting in breast cancer, which only touches the group's resistance and treatment-response interests and has no clear pathology, heterogeneity or model component.

articles.title: Impact of old age, comorbidity, and polypharmacy on adjuvant endocrine therapy for patients with early-stage breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A registry-based clinical study of adjuvant endocrine therapy benefit in older or comorbid women with early HR+ breast cancer has no pathology, biomarker, or tumor biology component, so it relates to the group's work only indirectly through the theme of treatment de-escalation.

articles.title: Perfluoroalkyl Substances and Estrogen Receptor‑Negative Breast Cancer: Looking Beyond Traditional Risk Factors.
articles.why_relevant: This appears to be a short commentary on environmental PFAS exposure and ER-negative breast cancer risk. It has no abstract and no pathology, AI, heterogeneity, resistance or model content, so it only touches the group's areas through ER status.

articles.title: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance Exposure and Breast Cancer Incidence in the Sister Study.
articles.why_relevant: This is an environmental epidemiology study of PFAS exposure and breast cancer risk, stratified only by ER status, and has no digital pathology, tumor heterogeneity, drug-resistance or patient-derived model component, so its relevance to the group's research is limited despite the high-impact journal.

articles.title: Evolving First-Line Treatment Strategies in ERBB2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Review.
articles.why_relevant: A review of first-line treatment in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer (DESTINY-Breast09, PATINA, HER2CLIMB-05) that touches on biomarker-driven selection (HER2DX, ctDNA) and biologic heterogeneity. It is useful background for the group's anti-HER2 resistance and treatment-prediction interests, but it is a clinical review with no new pathology or biomarker data.

articles.title: Treatment-related neutropenia as predictor of response to adjuvant palbociclib in the PALLAS trial (ABCSG-42/AFT-05/BIG-14-13/PrE0109).
articles.why_relevant: This exploratory analysis of a large phase III trial (PALLAS) tests a clinical pharmacodynamic marker (neutropenia) as a predictor of response to adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition, which touches the group's interest in predicting response beyond IHC markers. However, it uses no tissue, pathology or molecular data, and it is post hoc and subject to immortal-time and landmark bias.

articles.title: Global Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Cancer Mortality: An Analysis of 54 Countries.
articles.why_relevant: This is a population-level epidemiology study of COVID-19 effects on cancer mortality, with breast cancer as one of four cancer types and no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity or model component, so it barely touches the group's research.

articles.title: Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors.
articles.why_relevant: A Nature Genetics study using longitudinal single-cell RNA-seq, TCR sequencing and enhancer mapping on paired biopsies from patients on neoadjuvant aromatase inhibitors. It identifies resistance mechanisms (AR signaling, dedifferentiation, EMT, ineffective immune microenvironment) in patient material, which falls squarely within the group's focus on endocrine resistance, treatment prediction beyond routine IHC and intratumoral heterogeneity, although the cohort is small (n=25).

deep_analysis.central_finding: In ER-positive breast tumors under neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition, sensitivity was linked to high ER signaling and ER-bound enhancer activity, whereas resistance was linked to androgen receptor cis-regulome use, dedifferentiation, EMT and a 'hot' but ineffective immune microenvironment (naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells), while good responders showed an active microenvironment with sustained T-cell clonal expansion.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Longitudinal tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy were profiled with single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor (TCR) sequencing and enhancer activity mapping, and analyzed in relation to treatment response and tumor downstaging.
deep_analysis.limitation: The cohort is small (n=25), which limits statistical power and generalizability of the response-associated cellular, immune and epigenetic signatures.

articles.title: PELICAN-IPC 2015-016/Oncodistinct-003: A randomized non-comparative phase II study of pembrolizumab in combination with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in HER2-negative inflammatory breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A small randomized non-comparative phase II trial of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in HER2-negative inflammatory breast cancer. It touches on treatment response prediction through exploratory PD-L1, TIL and CTC biomarkers, none of which predicted pCR, so it is useful background on immunotherapy resistance and its lack of predictive markers, but it has no digital pathology or model component.

articles.title: Effects of digital stress-management interventions in breast cancer patients 18 months after intervention access.
articles.why_relevant: A psycho-oncology RCT of app-based stress management in breast cancer patients with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or model component, so it falls outside the group's research areas.

articles.title: Co-payments and adherence to endocrine therapy among Medicaid beneficiaries with breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This health-services study of co-payments and endocrine therapy adherence in Medicaid beneficiaries has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance-mechanism or model component, so it falls outside the group's translational research focus.

articles.title: A rare neurological adverse event of palbociclib: a chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) mimic.
articles.why_relevant: A single case report of a rare neurological adverse event with palbociclib; it has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, or resistance-mechanism component and only touches the CDK4/6 inhibitor setting.

articles.title: Clinicopathological differences between asymptomatic vs symptomatic breast cancer: a 30-year single-center retrospective study.
articles.why_relevant: A large single-center retrospective epidemiology and prognosis study of symptomatic versus asymptomatic presentation, with no digital pathology, molecular profiling, heterogeneity or model-system component, so it has only peripheral relevance to the group's focus on biomarkers and tumor biology.

articles.title: Male breast cancer: clinicopathological features and prevalence of germline pathogenic variants.
articles.why_relevant: A small retrospective descriptive cohort (n=106, germline testing in 55) of male breast cancer with clinicopathological features and germline variant prevalence; it has limited connection to the group's focus on digital pathology, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models, though germline and receptor-status data are marginally adjacent.

articles.title: Modeling neoadjuvant treatment plus additional therapy effects on US population breast cancer mortality.
articles.why_relevant: A CISNET population-level simulation of mortality benefit from response-guided post-neoadjuvant therapy with molecular subtype stratification; it relates only indirectly to treatment-response prediction and has no pathology, biomarker or model-system component.

articles.title: Overcoming platinum resistance by the disulfiram metabolite CuET in novel preclinical models of human carcinomas.
articles.why_relevant: Establishes platinum-resistant breast/lung cell lines and HGSOC patient-derived organoids and tests CuET to overcome chemoresistance, with IHC of TNBC and HGSOC tissue for candidate biomarkers (metallothioneins). This touches the group's interests in resistance, patient-derived models and biomarkers, but the work is mainly cell-line-based, not centred on breast cancer, and the patient validation is limited.

articles.title: An integrated breast cancer transcriptomic atlas defines clinical subtypes and informs cellular origin.
articles.why_relevant: A large harmonized transcriptomic atlas (7,612 tumors, 22 datasets) that refines intrinsic subtypes and identifies new subtypes (NED, BLP, HER2EKIS) with prognostic and treatment-response associations, directly relevant to molecular profiling and risk stratification beyond routine IHC, although it is based on aggregated public datasets with only partial independent clinical validation and no histopathology component.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Harmonizing bulk transcriptomes with single-cell-style analytical strategies produced a breast cancer atlas that recapitulates intrinsic subtypes and microenvironmental programs and identifies additional subtypes (stem-like, basal-luminal progenitor, mucinous, neuroendocrine-differentiated, and HER2EKIS), each with distinct prognostic or treatment-response associations.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Integrative analysis of 7,612 bulk breast cancer transcriptomes from 22 public datasets, harmonized with adapted single-cell RNA-seq methods, with subtype associations to clinical outcome after chemo-endocrine therapy and to neoadjuvant HER2-targeted kinase inhibitor response.
deep_analysis.limitation: The atlas relies on aggregated public bulk datasets with heterogeneous clinical annotation and only partial independent clinical validation, and bulk profiling cannot directly resolve cell-of-origin or intratumoral heterogeneity, so the origin inferences (e.g., bipotent or myoepithelial progenitor for BLP) are transcriptomic positioning rather than direct demonstration.

articles.title: Longitudinal Pancreatic Imaging Findings in BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM, and PALB2 Heterozygotes Undergoing Pancreatic Cancer Surveillance: A Prospective PRECEDE Consortium Study.
mesh_terms: Fanconi Anemia Complementation Group N Protein
articles.why_relevant: This is a pancreatic cancer imaging surveillance cohort in BRCA1/2, ATM and PALB2 carriers. It is not about breast cancer pathology, digital pathology, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models, so it only touches the group's areas through the shared germline genes.

articles.title: Brain as a site of first recurrence after adjuvant therapy for early breast cancer: mining the hellenic cooperative oncology group database-The BRACE study.
articles.why_relevant: A large retrospective clinical cohort on risk factors for brain metastasis at first recurrence (triple-negative subtype, nodal burden), using only clinicopathological variables and no digital pathology, molecular profiling or heterogeneity analysis, so it is only loosely related to the group's focus.

articles.title: Age-associated differences in the breast cancer immune microenvironment.
articles.why_relevant: A reasonably large, population-based IHC study of immune microenvironment markers (CD45, CD3, CD8, FOXP3, CD163, PD-L1) by age and prognosis in breast cancer; it is adjacent to the group's focus on biomarkers beyond routine IHC, but it uses manual or conventional IHC rather than AI, and has no resistance or model component.

articles.title: Co-targeting PARP and SHP2 Overcomes Resistance to Apoptosis and Induces Durable Responses in Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: It identifies adaptive resistance to anti-apoptotic (MCL1) inhibition in breast cancer and validates a PARP/SHP2 combination in cell lines and GEMMs, which is relevant to the group's interest in resistance mechanisms. However, it uses preclinical models without patient material or pathology/AI components, so it is mainly useful as background.

articles.title: Electronic health record embedded frailty index and outcomes among older adults receiving cancer chemotherapy.
articles.why_relevant: An EHR-based frailty index for older patients on chemotherapy (mixed lung, colorectal and breast cancer) has no pathology, tumor biology, biomarker or patient-derived model component, so it only touches the group's interest in risk stratification.

articles.title: Translating absolute risk of breast cancer into screening frequency: a framework to guide practice.
articles.why_relevant: A risk-model-agnostic framework mapping absolute breast cancer risk to mammography screening intervals is a screening and epidemiology paper with no pathology, tumor biology, or biomarker component, so it only tangentially touches the group's focus on risk assessment.

articles.title: Multicenter development and validation of a serum microRNA-based diagnostic model for breast cancer and its association with tumor burden and biological aggressiveness: an observational case-control study.
articles.why_relevant: A multicenter serum miRNA machine-learning diagnostic model for breast cancer detection with a held-out test set (AUC 0.875) and exploratory links to stage and grade; it is a liquid-biopsy screening study with no tissue, pathology-image, treatment-prediction or heterogeneity component, so it is only adjacent to the group's focus.

articles.title: Estimated global treatment costs for 31 cancer types by stage, year, and follow-up period: a systematic review and modelling study.
articles.why_relevant: A health-economics modelling study of global cancer treatment costs that has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived model component, so it only touches breast cancer as the largest cost driver.

articles.title: Risk stratification and potential overtreatment in adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor trials: do all patients with Stage II disease and favorable biology derive benefit?
articles.why_relevant: This commentary-style review addresses risk stratification by stage and tumour biology to avoid overtreatment with adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors, which fits the group's interest in treatment prediction beyond routine IHC, but it presents no new data, pathology methods or models.

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
articles.why_relevant: A surgical database study of postoperative VTE risk after breast cancer surgery with no pathology, tumor biology, biomarker, AI or patient-derived model component, so it has essentially no connection to the group's research.

articles.title: Acceptability of a patient support and educational intervention for black breast cancer survivors.
articles.why_relevant: A small feasibility study (n=20) of a psychosocial support and education intervention for Black breast cancer survivors, with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance or model component, so it falls outside the group's research.

articles.title: Glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B overexpression-a marker of resistance to cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 inhibitors.
articles.why_relevant: It identifies GPNMB as a CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance mechanism and candidate predictive biomarker in ER+ breast cancer, using drug-tolerant persister cell models, xenografts and comparison with PEARL trial data, and it suggests a therapeutic vulnerability (glembatumumab vedotin). This fits the group's focus on endocrine and CDK4/6 resistance and on predictors beyond routine IHC, though validation in patient tissue is limited.

deep_analysis.central_finding: GPNMB was upregulated in CDK4/6 inhibitor-resistant drug-tolerant persister ER+ breast cancer cells and in PEARL trial resistance-associated genes, and its overexpression in sensitive cells conferred resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition, increased migration and tumor growth, raised ITGB1/ITGA5 expression, and activated AKT and ERK signaling, while glembatumumab vedotin reduced viability of GPNMB-overexpressing cells and synergized with abemaciclib.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Abemaciclib- and palbociclib-tolerant persister derivatives of a panel of ER+ breast cancer cell lines were profiled with Clariom D transcriptomics (154 consistent resistance-associated genes) and compared with published PEARL trial resistance-associated genes, followed by in vitro and xenograft experiments with stable GPNMB overexpression in sensitive cells and glembatumumab vedotin treatment.
deep_analysis.limitation: Clinical relevance rests on overlap with published PEARL gene lists and on cell line and xenograft models with engineered overexpression, without direct validation of GPNMB protein expression as a predictive biomarker in patient tumor tissue.

articles.title: Safety and treatment duration of ribociclib + nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a phase 3 randomized controlled trial (NATALEE).
articles.why_relevant: This is a safety and tolerability analysis of the NATALEE phase 3 trial of adjuvant ribociclib, with no biomarker, pathology, heterogeneity or resistance-mechanism component, so it touches the group's interests only through CDK4/6 inhibitor context in HR+ breast cancer.

articles.title: Trichrome-based deep learning for quantitative assessment of steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
articles.why_relevant: A deep learning model on trichrome-stained liver biopsies for MASH, not breast cancer, with moderate external validation; it offers only general methodological background on quantitative whole-slide AI and external validation against pathologists.

articles.title: MONKEY Challenge: Machine-learning for Optimal detection of iNflammatory cells in KidnEY transplant biopsies.
articles.why_relevant: Not breast cancer, but a multicenter AI benchmark with IHC-restain-derived ground truth for inflammatory cell detection on routine stained slides, so the methodology (co-registered restaining, challenge design, compartment-specific quantification) is transferable to the group's work on TILs and clinical-grade AI tools.

articles.title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications.
articles.why_relevant: A systematic review of foundation and vision-language models in MRI, mostly neuroimaging, with no breast cancer or histopathology focus; it offers only loose conceptual parallels to pathology foundation models, such as multimodal integration and clinical translation challenges.

articles.title: Comparing Gleason pattern 4 measurement approaches on prostate biopsy using machine learning: a proof-of-principle study.
articles.why_relevant: Not breast cancer, but it uses a commercial clinical-grade AI tool (Paige) on digitized biopsy slides to compare quantification approaches for prognostic grading, which parallels the group's AI-based grading and risk assessment work; the modest discrimination (AUC ~0.65), convenience sample and proof-of-principle design limit its impact.

articles.title: Green Pathology: start small, think big. Awareness paper by the Advisory Board of the European Society of Pathology.
articles.why_relevant: An awareness paper on the environmental footprint of pathology labs, including the carbon cost of whole-slide imaging and AI, is tangentially relevant to the group's digital pathology implementation work but has no breast cancer, biomarker or methodological content.

articles.title: Ask Before You Look: A conversational multi-level pathology segmentation framework.
articles.why_relevant: A methods paper on language-guided pathology segmentation that reduces hallucination when the queried target is absent, which is relevant background for AI co-pilots in digital pathology, but it is not specific to breast cancer and shows no clinical validation or link to biomarkers or treatment prediction.

articles.title: Demonstrating the accuracy and efficiency of artificial intelligence integrated workflows for primary breast cancer diagnosis: A comparative paired reader analysis.
articles.why_relevant: This paired-reader study validates AI-assisted digital pathology in routine primary breast biopsy diagnosis, showing a 43.5% reduction in review time and maintained diagnostic accuracy. That is directly relevant to the group's work on implementing clinical-grade AI tools for H&E whole-slide images. It is limited by its single-site, retrospective design and small cohort (194 cases), and it does not address biomarker prediction.

deep_analysis.central_finding: AI-assisted digital pathology cut mean pathologist review time of primary breast biopsies by 43.5% (40.18 s vs 71.12 s, p < 0.0001) while maintaining diagnostic performance (agreement 99.48% with DP + AI vs 97.42% with DP alone), and standalone AI reached AUC ≥0.99 across cancer subtypes.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Retrospective, single-site, paired-reader, two-arm study of 194 consecutive digitized breast biopsies (DP vs DP + AI) against an adjudicated reference standard, plus a usability survey and a separate baseline turnaround-time analysis of 3298 cases with retrospective modelling of AI-guided IHC pre-ordering.
deep_analysis.limitation: The single-site, retrospective design with a small cohort of 194 cases limits generalizability. The projected ~2.5-day TAT reduction from AI-guided IHC pre-ordering comes from retrospective modelling on an independent cohort, not from a prospective test of the workflow.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound-based imaging modalities for assessing residual axillary lymph node disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.why_relevant: This meta-analysis covers ultrasound and radiomics for axillary restaging after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, which is a radiological question with no H&E pathology, molecular biomarker or patient-derived model component, so it is only tangentially related to the group's work and its AI evidence is sparse (3 studies).

articles.title: Two Niches, One Disease: Brain and Leptomeningeal Metastases in Breast Cancer: A Narrative Review.
articles.why_relevant: This narrative review compares brain parenchymal and leptomeningeal metastases in breast cancer, covering branched evolution, primary-metastasis and compartment discordance, biomarker representation and experimental modeling, which fits the group's interest in tumor-metastatic heterogeneity. It offers useful background but no original data, and it is published in a level 1 journal.

articles.title: DeMixNB: deconvolution of sparse-count RNA sequencing data for tumor cells using embedded negative binomial distributions.
articles.why_relevant: A deconvolution method for sparse-count data (miRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics) that estimates tumor-specific expression in bulk samples, applied to 885 breast cancer patients. It is adjacent to the group's work on intratumoral heterogeneity and spatial omics, but it is a computational-genomics tool with little pathology or treatment-response focus.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Microscopic Hyperspectral Images of HER2-Stained Breast Cancer Sections for Molecular Status Prediction.
articles.why_relevant: It applies weakly supervised deep learning to HER2 IHC assessment, which touches the group's interest in AI-based biomarker scoring. However, it uses only 43 cases, has no external validation, relies on specialised hyperspectral hardware that is not clinically deployable, and predicts binary HER2 status rather than HER2-low/ultralow or treatment response.

articles.title: Multi-omics of tertiary lymphoid structures in breast cancer: clinical significance and biomarker potential.
articles.why_relevant: A review of TLS as a prognostic and predictive biomarker in breast cancer, touching on histopathological classification, spatial multi-omics and standardisation problems that relate to the group's interest in biomarkers beyond routine IHC and in spatial heterogeneity, but it presents no new data and is a general overview.

articles.title: A deep learning model utilizing H&E-stained images for predicting HER2-low expression in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: The topic fits the group's interests (AI on H&E whole-slide images to predict HER2-low status beyond routine IHC), but the single-centre dataset, ImageNet ResNet50 with CLAM and AUC of only ~0.61 without external validation indicate weak performance and limited practical value, so it is worth skimming at most.

articles.title: Breast Cancer Screening in Rural West Texas: Access Barriers, Follow-Up Fragmentation, and AI-Enabled Oncology Care Delivery.
articles.why_relevant: A narrative review of rural screening access and care-delivery logistics, with AI discussed only for mammography and follow-up coordination; it has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity or patient-derived model content relevant to the group.

articles.title: Dual-organelle-coordinated sonodynamic nanoplatform amplifies immunogenic cell death to drive robust antitumor immunity in cold tumors.
articles.why_relevant: This is a nanomaterial sonodynamic therapy study in TNBC and PDAC. It uses patient-derived organoids and murine models but has no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity or resistance-mechanism angle, so it is only peripherally relevant to the group's focus.

articles.title: Promotion of the Proliferation and Migration of Breast Cancer Cells by the Micro Ribonucleic Acid miR-425-5p via Dihydropyrimidinase-Like 2.
articles.why_relevant: A mechanistic miRNA study (miR-425-5p/DPYSL2) in breast cancer cell lines, with only four patient-derived organoids and xenografts and mostly public-database expression data, so it has little connection to the group's focus on pathology, heterogeneity and treatment resistance.

articles.title: Single-cell Sequencing Reveals Multi-omics Dynamics During Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Single-cell multi-omics (genome, epigenome, transcriptome) of paired primary breast tumors and metastatic lymph nodes, with clonal evolution analysis, speaks directly to the group's interest in intratumoral heterogeneity and primary-metastasis discordance, though the cohort is likely small and the journal is level 1.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Single-cell multi-omics profiling of paired primary breast tumors and metastatic lymph nodes showed that a specific copy-number-defined clone has metastatic advantage in highly heterogeneous patients, that DNA methylation changes progressively across stages while transcriptional reprogramming concentrates at the tumor cell transition (suggesting microenvironment-driven remodelling), and that integrative analysis identified SLC39A6, ELP2 and RPL13 as dysregulated at multiple omic levels with relevance to metastasis or prognosis.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Simultaneous single-cell genome (copy number), epigenome (DNA methylation) and transcriptome sequencing of the same cells from paired primary tumors and metastatic lymph nodes of breast cancer patients, with clonal evolution analysis and integrative multi-omics analysis; the abstract does not state cohort size or independent validation cohorts.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract does not report the number of patients or an independent validation cohort, so the generalisability of the clonal and multi-omic findings and the evidence for the three candidate genes (SLC39A6, ELP2, RPL13) are unclear, and the microenvironment-remodelling interpretation is inferred rather than directly tested.

articles.title: Spatially resolved GR-TGFβ co-activation underlies cell-type-specific signalling in triple-negative breast cancer.
mesh_terms: Receptor, Transforming Growth Factor-beta Type II*
articles.why_relevant: Combines spatial transcriptomics, IHC and stereological single-cell co-localisation in human TNBC to show compartment-specific GR-TGFβ signalling, which fits the group's spatial heterogeneity theme. However, it is a mechanistic study in a level-1 journal that relies on public datasets for survival associations, and it has little connection to AI pathology, routine biomarkers or patient-derived models.
