articles.title: Early temporal transcriptional and cytokine responses distinguish chemotherapy sensitivity in patient-derived xenograft models of triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Uses serial sampling of TNBC PDX models to identify early transcriptional and cytokine signatures that separate chemoresponsive from chemoresistant tumors, with confirmation in paired on-treatment patient biopsies. This fits the group's interests in drug resistance, treatment-response prediction and patient-derived models, though the patient validation cohort is small and the work is not focused on imaging or AI.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Chemoresponsive and chemoresistant TNBC PDX models showed distinct transcriptional trajectories that diverged within one week of chemotherapy, before tumor volume changed, with chemoresponsive tumors activating apoptotic and cytokine/inflammatory pathways and myeloid cell infiltration that chemoresistant tumors lacked.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Serial fine needle aspirations with RNA-sequencing were performed on chemoresponsive and chemoresistant TNBC PDX models during chemotherapy, and the findings were compared with paired pre-treatment and early on-treatment (within four days of the first dose) biopsies from patients with TNBC.
deep_analysis.limitation: PDX models are grown in mice lacking a fully intact immune system, so the immune and microenvironment remodeling observed may not reflect immunocompetent human tumors, and the patient biopsy validation cohort is small.

articles.title: A Nationwide Study of Interobserver Agreement and Accuracy in HER2 Immunohistochemistry and the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on HER2 Interpretation.
articles.why_relevant: A large nationwide multireader study (34 pathologists, 168 WSIs) shows that AI assistance markedly improves interobserver agreement and sensitivity for HER2-low and HER2-ultralow scoring. This is directly relevant to the group's work on clinical-grade AI tools, IHC biomarker standardisation and beyond-routine HER2 assessment, although the journal is level 1 and the study uses a single assay and platform.

deep_analysis.central_finding: AI-assisted reading of HER2 IHC whole-slide images significantly improved interobserver agreement (Krippendorff's alpha 0.7415 to 0.8849; Fleiss' kappa 0.4492 to 0.7524) and sensitivity, most markedly for HER2-ultralow (48.5% to 73.9%) and IHC 1+ (64.9% to 87.7%) breast cancers.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Nationwide multireader study in which 34 board-certified breast pathologists scored 168 VENTANA HER2 (4B5)-stained breast cancer whole-slide images without AI, then again after a four-week washout with AI support, comparing agreement, classification performance and reading time.
deep_analysis.limitation: All cases were stained with a single assay (VENTANA 4B5) and digitized as WSIs, and the study used a single AI tool, so the findings may not generalize to other assays, scanners or platforms.

articles.title: SpatioCAD: Context-aware graph diffusion model for pinpointing spatially variable genes in heterogeneous tissues.
articles.why_relevant: A spatial transcriptomics method for detecting spatially variable genes that corrects for cell-density confounding in heterogeneous tumors, applied to breast cancer among other datasets, so it is relevant background for spatial heterogeneity work. It is primarily a computational methods paper with simulated and public data and no patient-material validation or treatment-response link.

articles.title: Enhancing cell type deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics through incorporating multiple reference panels.
articles.why_relevant: A statistical method for spatial transcriptomics deconvolution that integrates multiple scRNA-seq references and is applied to breast cancer to resolve tumor, stromal and immune compartments, which is useful background for spatial heterogeneity work. It is methods-focused, only partly breast-specific, and shows no patient-cohort validation or link to treatment response.

articles.title: Multi-task Model with​ Peritumoral MRI Radiomics Learning for Breast Cancer Segmentation-Guided Subtype Classification.
articles.why_relevant: This is a retrospective single-center MRI radiomics and deep learning study predicting molecular subtype. It is not histopathology, has no external validation, and sits only adjacent to the group's AI-based biomarker prediction work.

articles.title: TRACER: Twin-contrastive learning for fine-grained and rare spatial domain identification in spatial transcriptomics.
articles.why_relevant: A spatial transcriptomics domain-identification method that touches on intratumoral spatial heterogeneity (it finds small functional domains in one breast cancer section), but it is mainly benchmarked on brain datasets and has no clinical or pathology validation, so it is useful methodological background only.

articles.title: From staging to changing strategy: [18F]FDG PET/MRI's impact on treatment planning in early breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A prospective single-arm imaging study on how FDG PET/MRI staging changes treatment planning in early breast cancer; it has no pathology, biomarker, AI or model component, so it is only tangentially related to the group's focus (multifocality aside).

articles.title: Cancer in Seychelles: A Population-Based Study on Incidence, Trends and Stage at Diagnosis (2005-2024).
articles.why_relevant: A population-based cancer registry study on incidence trends and stage at diagnosis in Seychelles with no biomarker, pathology, AI, heterogeneity, resistance or model component, so it only touches breast cancer epidemiology.

articles.title: Is Ductal Carcinoma In Situ a Precursor or Low-Risk Variant of Invasive Breast Cancer? A Population Perspective.
articles.why_relevant: A population-level epidemiological perspective on whether DCIS is a precursor or a low-risk variant of invasive breast cancer; it touches on tumor biology and overtreatment but has no pathology, AI, biomarker or model component that connects directly to the group's methods.

articles.title: Time-dependent anti-Müllerian hormone dynamics during GnRHa-based endocrine therapy in young breast cancer survivors: a longitudinal real-world cohort study.
articles.why_relevant: A retrospective clinical cohort on AMH dynamics and ovarian reserve in young breast cancer survivors on GnRHa therapy, with no pathology, tumor biology, resistance or heterogeneity component, so it is only marginally related to the group's research.

articles.title: Longitudinal trajectories of menopausal symptoms in women receiving endocrine therapy for breast cancer compared with natural menopause.
articles.why_relevant: This is a patient-reported outcome study of menopausal symptom burden during endocrine therapy, with no pathology, biomarker, heterogeneity, resistance-mechanism or model component, so it is only marginally related to the group's research.

articles.title: Drugging the luminal axis end to end: A review of next-generation endocrine and targeted therapies in HR + /HER2- metastatic breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A review of next-generation endocrine and targeted therapies in HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer, organized around resistance mechanisms (ESR1 mutation, PI3K, CDK4/6, CDK2) and biomarker-guided selection via tissue and ctDNA, which is useful background for the group's endocrine resistance work but offers no new data or pathology/AI angle.

articles.title: From TAILORx to OPTIMA: Evolving Evidence for Genomically Guided Chemotherapy in Hormone Receptor-Positive Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: The title suggests a review or commentary on genomic assays (Oncotype DX in TAILORx, Prosigna in OPTIMA) for guiding chemotherapy in HR+/HER2- breast cancer, which is relevant background to the group's work on risk assessment beyond routine IHC, but no abstract or original data is available and it is likely an editorial or review.

articles.title: Vascular normalization confers an endothelial immune suppressive gene expression profile.
articles.why_relevant: A mouse breast cancer model with endothelial Shb deficiency, supported by public human endothelial expression data, suggests that vascular normalization produces an immunosuppressive endothelial profile; this is tangential to the group's focus on pathology, heterogeneity, resistance and patient-derived models, and has no direct biomarker or digital pathology angle.

articles.title: CK2 targeting potentiates antineoplastic effects of dual HER2/EGFR inhibitor lapatinib and attenuates growth factor-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
articles.why_relevant: It addresses endocrine and anti-HER2 resistance mechanisms (CK2/ERK/cyclin D1, EMT, lapatinib sensitization), which fits the group's resistance theme, but the evidence comes from cell lines plus public dataset analysis, with no patient-material, organoid or PDX validation.

articles.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial.
articles.why_relevant: A Nat Med phase 2 trial of response-adapted de-escalation in HER2-positive breast cancer, with exploratory ctDNA analyses that predict pCR and long-term outcome, so it is relevant to treatment-response prediction beyond routine IHC. It is mainly a clinical imaging- and pCR-guided trial with no pathology, AI or tissue-based heterogeneity component, so it is background rather than core for the group.

articles.title: WHO releases framework for expanding access to early breast cancer care.
articles.why_relevant: A short news item on a WHO framework for access to early breast cancer care, with no abstract, data, or pathology, biomarker, AI, or model content, so it only touches the group's field at a health-policy level.

articles.title: Knowledge gaps and future perspectives for the definition, diagnostics and treatment of isolated locoregional recurrent breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A clinical review of isolated locoregional recurrence covering definition, work-up and treatment; it touches on distinguishing true recurrence from a second primary (a clonality/heterogeneity question), but it has no pathology, AI or biomarker data and is only tangential to the group's work.

articles.title: Real-world efficacy and safety of trastuzumab emtansine biosimilar (UJVIRA®) in early and metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer: a multicenter pooled retrospective analysis from India.
articles.why_relevant: A retrospective real-world study of a T-DM1 biosimilar in HER2-positive breast cancer, with no biomarker, pathology, heterogeneity or resistance-mechanism analysis, so it only touches the group's anti-HER2 therapy interest.

articles.title: Sociodemographic and clinicopathologic features associated with rapid relapse in triple-negative breast cancer: a Swedish nationwide registry-based study.
articles.why_relevant: A large Swedish nationwide registry study of rapid versus late relapse in TNBC that touches on risk stratification, but it uses only routine clinicopathologic and sociodemographic variables with no digital pathology, molecular, or model-based biomarker component.

articles.title: Invasive Lobular Carcinoma With Extracellular Mucin Production: First Whole Exome Sequencing of a Rare Histological Variant of Breast Carcinoma.
articles.why_relevant: This is the first whole-exome sequencing of a rare ILC variant, including matched lymph node metastases, and it clarifies the molecular classification and potentially targetable alterations; however, the cohort is very small (7 patients) and it has no AI, model or resistance component, so it is mainly useful background on genomics and histological subtyping.

articles.title: To stop or not to stop? International physician survey on HER2 targeted therapy for metastatic breast cancer patients in remission.
articles.why_relevant: A physician opinion survey on stopping maintenance HER2-targeted therapy in HER2+ MBC patients in remission; it touches anti-HER2 therapy but has no biomarker, pathology, heterogeneity or resistance-mechanism data.

articles.title: Extracellular matrix stiffness controls Transposable Elements through Pin1 to promote immune evasion in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A high-impact mechanistic study of ECM stiffness-driven immune evasion and checkpoint-blockade sensitization in breast cancer (Pin1/TE/cGAS-STING), which touches on immunotherapy resistance and tumor microenvironment heterogeneity, but it is largely preclinical and has no digital pathology, patient-derived model or routine biomarker angle.

articles.title: Neuroendocrine Differentiation Mediates Escape from HER2-Targeted Therapy in Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Identifies neuroendocrine differentiation as a new mechanism of escape from anti-HER2 therapy, validated in progressive patient cases and in patient-derived organoid and xenograft models. It also addresses primary-metastasis phenotypic divergence and HER2 loss, which are core themes for the group (resistance mechanisms, heterogeneity, patient-derived models), and it was published in a top-tier journal.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Neuroendocrine differentiation emerges or increases in about 22% of progressive breast cancers, mainly HER2-positive, and drives escape from HER2-targeted therapy through epigenetic silencing of EpCAM and amplified HER2, NEUROD1-driven neuroendocrine fate, and FGFR1 dependency.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Analysis of progressive patient cases (neuroendocrine features in 22%) combined with patient-derived epithelial and neuroendocrine organoid and xenograft models, used for epigenetic and transcriptional profiling to define a neuroendocrine signature, plus detection of NCAM-positive putative circulating tumor cells in patients where EpCAM-based detection failed.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract gives no cohort sizes or independent validation cohorts, and the mechanistic findings (NEUROD1 regulation, FGFR1 dependency) rest on a limited number of patient-derived models, so generalizability across breast cancer subtypes and patients is uncertain.

articles.title: Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study.
articles.why_relevant: A large prospective ctDNA surveillance study in high-risk ER+/HER2- early breast cancer (Ann Oncol) that gives molecular relapse rates and detection factors and is adjacent to the group's focus on risk assessment beyond routine IHC. It is a liquid-biopsy trial rather than pathology, AI or patient-derived models, and the treatment-intervention results are not yet reported.

articles.title: CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore predict individual outcomes but not trial results after neoadjuvant therapy for early breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Large pooled analysis (8,359 patients, nine GBG/AGO-B trials) validates post-neoadjuvant prognostic scores that combine pathology and biology (CPS+EG, Neo-Bioscore) and shows they work for individual risk but not as trial-level surrogates, which bears directly on risk assessment and neoadjuvant response prediction beyond routine IHC, although it has no digital pathology or model component.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Both CPS+EG and Neo-Bioscore were significantly associated with long-term outcomes at the individual patient level, but their trial-level associations with DDFS, iDFS and OS were weak (R² 0.03–0.24 with wide confidence intervals), so neither qualifies as a surrogate endpoint for long-term treatment benefit.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Pooled surrogacy analysis of 8,359 patients from nine randomized neoadjuvant trials run by the German Breast Group and AGO-B, assessing patient-level and trial-level associations of the two post-neoadjuvant scores with DDFS, iDFS and OS.
deep_analysis.limitation: Trial-level surrogacy estimates are imprecise, with wide confidence intervals, because they rest on only nine trials, which limits how firmly the lack of surrogacy can be established.

articles.title: The right drug, the wrong assay: TROP2-ADC assessment in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: The title suggests a commentary on assay choice for assessing TROP2 as a predictive biomarker for ADCs in breast cancer, which touches the group's interest in biomarkers beyond routine IHC and in ADC response. No abstract or data are available, and it is likely a short opinion piece, so it is worth skimming only.

articles.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus chemotherapy in previously treated locally recurrent or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer: final overall survival analysis of the Phase III OptiTROP-Breast01.
articles.why_relevant: A high-impact phase III final OS analysis of the TROP2 ADC sac-TMT in pretreated TNBC, relevant background for ADC resistance and response prediction, but it is a clinical trial report without biomarker, pathology or heterogeneity analyses.

articles.title: Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2- breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial.
articles.why_relevant: A large, positive phase 3 trial of an EGFR/HER3 bispecific ADC in heavily pretreated HR+/HER2- breast cancer; it is relevant background for ADC resistance and target-expression heterogeneity, but it is a clinical efficacy trial with no pathology or biomarker analysis in the abstract (HER2 status is only a stratification factor).

articles.title: There is beauty after breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A short piece with no abstract, apparently a non-research commentary, with no apparent link to the group's work on digital pathology, biomarkers, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models.

articles.title: Tumor digital twins uncover therapeutic strategies in triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A mechanistic digital-twin framework for TNBC that predicts treatment response and resistance mechanisms from patient-specific molecular data, validated on clinical trial data (PARTNER). This fits the group's interest in treatment prediction beyond routine IHC and in resistance and clonal evolution, but it is molecular rather than pathology- or image-based.

deep_analysis.central_finding: A mechanistic qualitative network-based digital twin of TNBC, parameterized with patient-specific molecular data, predicts treatment response, identifies resistance mechanisms and mutational and transcriptional biomarkers of outcome, and proposes tailored treatment plans to overcome resistance.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: The model is a prior-knowledge-based network with genes and proteins as nodes and their interactions as edges, and it was validated on clinical and molecular data from the randomized PARTNER trial of platinum-based chemotherapy with or without PARP inhibitor.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract describes validation only in the PARTNER trial cohort and reports no image or pathology input, so the model's generalizability to other cohorts and its handling of spatial or clonal heterogeneity are not shown.

articles.title: Tailoring adjuvant endocrine therapy in patients with estrogen receptor-low breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: ER-low breast cancer sits at the edge of routine ER IHC interpretation and its predictive value for endocrine therapy, which fits the group's interest in biomarkers beyond standard IHC. No abstract is available, so the study design and strength of evidence cannot be judged, and it may be a short commentary or letter.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist-associated weight loss in breast cancer patients receiving concurrent endocrine therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis.
articles.why_relevant: A retrospective clinical cohort on GLP-1 RA weight loss during endocrine therapy with no pathology, AI, heterogeneity, resistance-mechanism or model component; the only link is an incidental PR-status subgroup finding.

articles.title: Circulating tumor cells in lobular versus ductal metastatic breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Compares CTC burden between lobular and ductal metastatic breast cancer in two validated cohorts, which touches on metastatic biology and histotype-specific differences. It has no pathology, AI or model component and uses only CellSearch counts, so it is background reading for the group.

articles.title: Efficacy and toxicity for pembrolizumab-containing therapy in older adults with triple-negative breast cancer: insights from routine oncology practice.
articles.why_relevant: A retrospective real-world study of pembrolizumab toxicity and efficacy in older TNBC patients with no biomarker, pathology or heterogeneity component, so it is only tangentially related to the group's focus on treatment prediction beyond routine markers.

articles.title: Risk of malignancy after diagnosis of radial sclerosing lesion with associated atypia.
articles.why_relevant: A single-institution cohort on upgrade risk of radial sclerosing lesions with atypia on core biopsy, which touches breast pathology and risk stratification but has no molecular, AI or heterogeneity component and concerns benign/high-risk lesions rather than the group's focus on tumor biology and treatment prediction.

articles.title: Mind the Gap: Continuous magnification sampling for pathology foundation models.
articles.why_relevant: A methods paper in a top-level journal on how magnification sampling affects pathology foundation models, with new benchmarks (including breast-based BRACS-MS) and a comparison of current models, which is useful for a group building and validating clinical-grade H&E AI tools. It is not breast-specific and offers no direct clinical validation, so it stops short of a must-read.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Framing magnification sampling as multi-source domain adaptation, the authors show that discrete uniform sampling (0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 mpp) degrades performance at intermediate magnifications, whereas continuous magnification sampling closes these gaps, keeps performance at standard scales, and improves balanced accuracy by up to 4 percentage points, with optimized sampling distributions giving further gains.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Theoretical framework plus empirical training and evaluation of pathology foundation models on two newly introduced multi-scale benchmarks (TCGA-MS and the breast-derived BRACS-MS) with dedicated metrics, and a benchmark comparison of current histopathology foundation models across magnifications.
deep_analysis.limitation: The evidence comes from benchmark-based downstream classification tasks derived from TCGA and BRACS, with no clinical or prospective validation, so the findings may not generalize to other tissues or real-world diagnostic settings.

articles.title: Computational image features of immune architecture reveal molecular patterns associated with outcome and risk of recurrence in microsatellite-stable or MSI-low colon cancers.
articles.why_relevant: Not breast cancer, but a well-validated H&E whole-slide image framework (external cohorts, benchmarked against eight foundation-model MIL approaches) that quantifies spatial TIL architecture for risk prediction, which is methodologically relevant to the group's AI-based risk assessment work.

articles.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.
articles.why_relevant: A high-impact multimodal vision-language foundation model with explainability, validated across 10 imaging modalities and including pathology, is a methods advance the group could compare against for clinical-grade AI. It is not breast cancer- or H&E-specific, and pathology is only one of six specialties, so direct applicability is limited.

articles.title: Deep learning predicts IDH1 mutation status in acute myeloid leukemia from bone marrow smears.
articles.why_relevant: Not breast cancer, but it uses attention-based multiple-instance learning on whole-slide images to predict a mutation, with multicenter data (436 patients, 4 centers) and an interpretability analysis; this is methodologically close to the group's AI-on-histopathology work for molecular prediction, though the cytology/hematology setting and moderate AUC (0.81) limit direct applicability.

articles.title: Interpretable deep learning maps spatial morphological phenotypes to HCC and LUAD survival.
articles.why_relevant: Although it covers HCC and LUAD rather than breast cancer, this multi-center, externally validated, interpretable H&E whole-slide image survival model links nuclear and texture morphology to biology and heterogeneity, which fits the group's AI-based risk assessment work and could serve as a methodological comparator.

deep_analysis.central_finding: MorphX, an interpretable framework that fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics from H&E whole-slide images, predicts survival in HCC and LUAD (C-index 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts) and yields eight morphology-based biomarkers (texture heterogeneity in necrotic regions, lymphocyte density, nuclear shape) with reproducible survival associations across independent cohorts.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Multi-center retrospective study of 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma and lung adenocarcinoma using H&E whole-slide images, with model development in discovery cohorts and testing of the derived biomarkers in independent cohorts.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract reports C-indices only for discovery cohorts and gives no external-cohort performance figures, and the study covers only HCC and LUAD, so generalisability beyond these tumour types (including breast cancer) is untested.

articles.title: Learning discriminative prototypes via Variational Information Bottleneck for multimodal cancer survival prediction.
articles.why_relevant: A multimodal WSI-genomics MIL method for survival prediction that is relevant to the group's computational pathology work, but it is validated only on TCGA cohorts across several cancer types, with no independent validation and no breast-specific or clinical-grade focus.

articles.title: FGFR Alterations in Bladder Cancer-From Molecular Pathogenesis to Precision Oncology.
articles.why_relevant: A review of FGFR biomarkers and targeted therapy in bladder cancer, with only a passing mention of AI-assisted pathology. It is not about breast cancer, and the group's focus on computational pathology, heterogeneity or patient-derived models is touched on only marginally, so it is general precision-oncology background.

articles.title: Beyond a single ratio: an adaptable deep learning approach to analyze the prognostic value of TSP distribution in ovarian cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A deep learning pipeline on H&E whole-slide images that quantifies the whole-tumor distribution of tumor-stroma percentage as a spatial heterogeneity biomarker, which fits the group's AI-pathology and heterogeneity interests. However, it is in ovarian cancer with only 98 patients and no clear external validation, so it is useful mainly as methodological background.

articles.title: Histopathology-Based Spatial Profiling of Immune and Molecular Features Predicts Cancer Risk in Barrett's Esophagus Patients.
articles.why_relevant: Not breast cancer, but a well-validated multi-institution deep learning study on routine H&E that predicts a molecular feature (DNA content) and spatial immune ecology to stratify risk. This is close to the group's work on AI-based prediction of molecular and risk information from whole-slide images and on spatial heterogeneity.

deep_analysis.central_finding: BEACON, a framework that combines deep learning prediction of DNA content abnormality (DACOR) from H&E with spatial immune ecology metrics such as plasma cell clustering next to abnormal epithelium, stratified DNA-content-abnormal Barrett's esophagus patients into high- and low-risk groups that corresponded with cancer progression and survival.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: DACOR, a multi-instance learning model, was trained on 777 BE biopsies with flow cytometry DNA content data scanned at two institutions and evaluated on validation and test sets; cell classification and tissue segmentation models then supplied immune spatial metrics, which were combined with molecular and epithelial morphology features in a logistic regression risk model.
deep_analysis.limitation: The abstract does not describe independent external validation of the integrated risk model or the size of the progressor cohort, so the generalizability of the risk stratification is unclear, and the plasma cell clustering finding rests on associations within a subset of DNA-content-abnormal patients.

articles.title: RF-based ultrasound elastography image reconstruction using biomechanically informed deep learning.
articles.why_relevant: This is a deep-learning ultrasound elastography reconstruction study trained on finite-element simulated data. It does not involve histopathology, molecular biomarkers, heterogeneity, resistance or patient-derived models, so it only touches the group's interests through the use of breast cancer AI.

articles.title: Virtual IHC Synthesis and Bimodal Fusion for Patch-Level Classification of HER2 IHC Expression in Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: It predicts HER2 IHC categories (0/1+/2+/3+) from H&E using virtual staining and bimodal fusion, which fits the group's AI-on-H&E work beyond routine IHC. However, the cohort is small (48 patients, single centre), there is no independent validation, and patch-level accuracy is modest (67%), so it is only worth skimming.

articles.title: Breast cancer adaptation to oxygen stress: mechanisms of tumor survival, progression, and therapeutic resistance.
articles.why_relevant: A narrative review on hypoxia and oxygen-stress adaptation as a driver of resistance to endocrine and HER2-directed therapy, touching on spatial and subtype heterogeneity. It is useful background for the group's resistance and heterogeneity work, but it presents no new data, patient-material validation or pathology/AI component.

articles.title: ATAD2B governs epigenetic silencing of the epithelial program to fuel cancer metastasis and neuronal migration.
articles.why_relevant: A mechanistic study of epigenetic control of EMT and metastasis that uses breast cancer lines, patient-derived organoids and in vivo lung metastasis, which touches the group's interest in metastatic biology and patient-derived models, but it is not about pathology, biomarkers or treatment response.

articles.title: An interpretable deep learning framework for revealing fine-grained spatial domains.
articles.why_relevant: A spatial transcriptomics domain-identification method that is also applied to breast cancer datasets (a hypoxic, T-cell-suppressed microenvironment and an EMT gradient in IDC with over 720,000 cells), which is useful background for spatial heterogeneity work, but it is a general computational methods paper with no H&E, patient-material validation or treatment-response link.

articles.title: DiST: disentangling structure via self-supervised tensors for heterophilous spatial transcriptomics.
articles.why_relevant: A spatial transcriptomics domain-identification method, validated on human breast cancer data, that could help the group study spatial and functional heterogeneity. It is a general computational methods paper with limited breast-specific validation and no link to treatment response or histopathology.

articles.title: Ki67 assessment, digital image analysis, and PAM50/Prosigna subtype divergence in early ER-positive breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: Directly addresses the group's core question of going beyond routine IHC (Ki67 reproducibility, digital Ki67 image analysis) by comparing surrogate subtyping with PAM50/Prosigna in ER-positive early breast cancer, though it is a modest-sized single-cohort study in a level 1 journal.

deep_analysis.central_finding: IHC-based surrogate subtyping and Prosigna PAM50 intrinsic subtyping diverged in 34% of early ER-positive breast cancers (26 IHC Luminal B cases reclassified as Luminal A or HER2-enriched, 8 Luminal A cases reclassified as Luminal B), with divergence concentrated in a Ki67 'grey zone' of 16-30% and peaking at 21-25%.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Single-cohort retrospective comparison of IHC-derived subtypes (ER, PR, HER2, Ki67) with Prosigna PAM50 subtypes in early-stage breast cancer cases, with divergence analysed across Ki67 cut-off bands; the abstract does not give the total cohort size and reports no independent validation cohort.
deep_analysis.limitation: The cohort is modest and from a single centre, and the abstract does not show that second-pathologist review or digital Ki67 analysis were tested directly, so their suggested benefit for reproducibility is not demonstrated by the reported results.

articles.title: HER2-low and HER2-ultralow breast cancer in the antibody-drug conjugate era: diagnostic challenges and reporting workflow.
articles.why_relevant: A pathology-centered review of HER2-low/ultralow scoring, IHC interobserver variability, intratumoral heterogeneity and reporting workflow in the ADC era, which is directly adjacent to the group's biomarker and digital-scoring interests, but it is a narrative review with no new data and was published in a level 1 journal.

articles.title: RAMP3 is associated with macrophage-driven immune exclusion and promotes resistance to PD-1 blockade in breast cancer: integrated in vivo and single-cell transcriptomic analyses.
articles.why_relevant: It proposes a macrophage-mediated mechanism of resistance to PD-1 blockade in breast cancer, but the evidence comes from syngeneic mouse models, scRNA-seq and public datasets (TCGA, public spatial data) with no validation in patient material, and the topic is only loosely connected to the group's focus on endocrine/anti-HER2 resistance and pathology.

articles.title: Assessment of Metastatic Dissemination in Mouse Breast Carcinoma Models Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI).

articles.title: Spatial context-aware breast cancer molecular subtype prediction in whole-slide images using graph convolutional networks: Cross-domain evaluation.
articles.why_relevant: It compares graph-based spatial context with attention-based aggregation for predicting molecular subtype from H&E whole-slide images, with cross-domain testing (biopsy to resection) and foundation model (CONCH) integration, all directly relevant to the group's AI-on-H&E work, though the journal is level 1 and accuracy is modest.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Graph-convolutional, spatial context-aware aggregation of H&E whole-slide image features significantly outperformed non-context-aware attention pooling for molecular subtype prediction within-domain (accuracy gains of +4.6 to +9.2 percentage points), but this advantage did not persist under biopsy-to-resection domain shift or with CONCH foundation model features.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Controlled comparison of WSI2Graph-based spatial KNN graph aggregation versus attention-based pooling under identical feature extraction, using three evaluation protocols: within-domain on BCNB (1058 core-needle biopsies), constrained cross-domain transfer to SBC (533 surgical resections), and CONCH foundation model integration, with McNemar's paired tests, ablations, and interpretability analyses.
deep_analysis.limitation: The ablation indicates that aggregator capacity explains a substantial part of the within-domain context-aware advantage, so the gain cannot be attributed purely to spatial context, and cross-domain transfer was tested on only one biopsy-to-resection dataset pair with inconsistent task-dependent results.

articles.title: Lymph node whole-slide images provide incremental value beyond primary tumors for AI-based pCR prediction in node-positive breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: A large (n=1812) AI study on paired H&E whole-slide images of primary tumor and lymph node for neoadjuvant pCR prediction, with external validation, comparison against an IHC-based model, and transcriptomic evidence of primary-metastasis differences. This fits the group's interests in AI-based treatment prediction beyond routine IHC and in tumor-metastatic heterogeneity, though the journal is lower-tier and the external validation is only preliminary.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Adding a lymph node whole-slide image model (N-Net) to a primary tumor model (P-Net) via decision-level fusion (DP-Net) improved AI-based pCR prediction in node-positive breast cancer (AUROC 0.814 vs 0.793 for P-Net alone), and the gain persisted when combined with an IHC-Age model (AUROC 0.869 vs 0.855).
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Retrospective study of 1812 node-positive breast cancer patients treated with neoadjuvant therapy, using paired H&E whole-slide images of primary tumor and lymph node biopsies, with internal validation, a preliminary external validation cohort, attention heatmaps, and transcriptomic comparison of primary tumors and lymph node metastases.
deep_analysis.limitation: The external validation cohort was only preliminary and the study was retrospective, so the generalizability of the modest AUROC gains (about 0.02 over P-Net and 0.014 over IHC-Age) is uncertain.

articles.title: Longitudinal Spatial Proteomics of Breast Cancer Reveals Recurrent Phenotypic Clone States and Temporal Trajectories.
articles.why_relevant: Longitudinal, pathologist-guided spatial proteomics (MALDI-MSI plus dia-PASEF) on paired primary, relapse and metastatic FFPE breast cancer tissue maps intratumoral heterogeneity and state turnover during therapy, which is directly within the group's heterogeneity and primary-metastasis focus, though the cohort is small (16 patients) and has no external validation.

deep_analysis.central_finding: Integrating MALDI-MSI with region-resolved dia-PASEF proteomics identified 10 recurrent spatial proteomic states that recur across breast cancer subtypes and show marked turnover during therapy, with some states persisting and others emerging at relapse or metastasis, and with exploratory shifts from immune- and hormone-associated programs toward inflammatory, invasive and stress-adapted programs.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Forty-seven FFPE tissues from 16 patients (primary, relapse and metastatic lesions; HR-positive, HER2-positive and HR-negative/HER2-low) underwent cohort-level MSI co-segmentation, and pathologist-guided microextraction of 201 tumor regions gave 402 dia-PASEF proteomic datasets, analyzed with feature-ranking models and exploratory enrichment analyses, without an external validation cohort.
deep_analysis.limitation: The cohort is small, repeated regions from the same patient are not independent, there is no genomic lineage tracing (so states are not proven clones) and no external validation, so all predictive and trajectory interpretations are hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Spatially dissecting drivers of inter- and intra-tumoral heterogeneity in Kenyan breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This study directly addresses intratumoral heterogeneity in breast cancer using spatial protein profiling across multiple regions, demonstrating that bulk profiling obscures tumor complexity and that over one-third of tumors show marked ITH including multiple co-existing intrinsic subtypes—highly relevant to the group's work on spatial heterogeneity, receptor discordance, and the limitations of standard IHC biomarkers.

deep_analysis.central_finding: All 31 Kenyan breast tumors showed measurable intra-tumoral heterogeneity (ITH) in protein marker expression, with one-third exhibiting marked heterogeneity and over half harbouring two or more co-existing intrinsic subtypes, while AOI tissue phenotype (epithelium- vs. stroma-rich) was the primary driver of marker variability and bulk profiling was shown to obscure or misrepresent this complexity.
deep_analysis.design_and_data: Cross-sectional spatial profiling study of 31 primary breast tumors from Kenyan patients, quantifying 44 protein markers across 707 PanCK-segmented Areas of Illumination (AOIs) using NanoString GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler, with comparisons to InSituPlex multiplex immunofluorescence and bulk RNA data; linear mixed-effects modelling used to partition sources of variance.
deep_analysis.limitation: The cohort is small (n=31 tumors) and derived from a single institution in Kenya, limiting statistical power and generalisability, and over 25% residual marker variability remained unexplained by all measured spatial and biological covariates, indicating unmeasured biological or microenvironmental factors are not captured by the current platform or model.

articles.title: Performance of Naïve Spectral Geometric Models in Histopathology AI.
articles.why_relevant: While this benchmarks spectral geometric methods for histopathology AI (including breast cancer classification on BreaKHis), the methods underperform CNN baselines and the study lacks clinical validation or whole-slide image analysis at the scale relevant to the group's work.

articles.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission Nanoassembly with Enhanced Radiosensitization for Boosting Breast Cancer Radiotherapy.
articles.why_relevant: Although patient-derived organoids are used for validation, the study's focus is on a novel radiosensitizing nanoparticle platform for radiotherapy—outside the group's core areas of AI pathology, biomarkers, heterogeneity, and resistance to endocrine/anti-HER2 therapies.

articles.title: Breast cancer cells with decreased fibronectin-integrin adhesion strength attenuate the malignancy of its microenvironment.
articles.why_relevant: While the organoid component and tumor microenvironment findings are of some interest, this study focuses on fibronectin-integrin mechanobiology in mouse models rather than the group's core areas of AI pathology, molecular biomarkers, treatment resistance, or patient-derived models for drug testing.

articles.title: Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled Heterodimers for Dual Integrin αvβ3 and PARP1-Targeted Tumor Imaging.
articles.why_relevant: This study focuses on radiopharmaceutical development for PET imaging of integrin αvβ3 and PARP1, with no connection to the group's core areas of digital pathology, histopathology AI, tumor heterogeneity characterization, or patient-derived models.

articles.title: A Senescence-Related Signature for Risk Stratification and Predicted Immunotherapy Response in Breast Cancer: Integrative Pathology and Multi-Omics Analysis.
articles.why_relevant: Although this study integrates H&E image features and multi-omics for breast cancer prognostic stratification, it relies primarily on TCGA data mining without independent patient cohort validation, and its focus on senescence signatures and immunotherapy prediction is peripheral to the group's core areas of AI pathology grading, HER2/ER/PR biomarkers, drug resistance mechanisms, and patient-derived models.

articles.title: Reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages in breast cancer: from myeloid plasticity and tumor-promoting programs to CAR-macrophage therapy.
articles.why_relevant: This review on tumor-associated macrophage biology and CAR-M therapy in breast cancer touches on spatial and single-cell heterogeneity of the TME, but the group's focus is on pathology AI, molecular profiling, drug resistance mechanisms, and patient-derived models rather than macrophage immunology or immunotherapy.

articles.title: Benchmark Evaluation of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Mammography: A Case-Control Study.
articles.why_relevant: Evaluates AI/LLM performance on mammography images rather than histopathology whole-slide images, making it only peripherally related to the group's focus on H&E-based digital pathology and tumor biology.

articles.title: Raman spectroscopy reveals a novel mechanism by which cyclin Y promotes breast cancer progression by regulating lipid metabolism.
articles.why_relevant: While PDX models are used for validation, the study focuses on a novel cyclin (CCNY) and lipid metabolism mechanism with limited direct connection to the group's core areas of AI pathology, heterogeneity, or treatment resistance/prediction.

articles.title: Profiling protein post-translational modifications in plasma-derived extracellular vesicles as fingerprints for breast cancer subtypes.
articles.why_relevant: Identifies post-translational modification signatures in plasma extracellular vesicles for breast cancer subtype differentiation (including HER2, TNBC, luminal), with PAM50 alignment and machine learning validation, offering a liquid biopsy angle that is adjacent to the group's molecular profiling and subtype biomarker work but not directly focused on histopathology, AI on WSI, or patient-derived models.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal that THBS1 induces radiation resistance in TNBC through the interaction between myCAF and TOPBP1⁺ tumor cells.
articles.why_relevant: While it uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to study resistance mechanisms in TNBC, the focus is on radiotherapy resistance via tumor-stroma (myCAF-TOPBP1⁺ cell) interactions, which is peripheral to the group's main focus on endocrine, anti-HER2, and CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance, and the study lacks strong independent patient cohort validation.

articles.title: A multi-omics study integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and mendelian randomization unveil the implication of TRDMT1 expression in T cells on the immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: While the study uses spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA-seq in breast cancer, its focus on an RNA methylation writer (TRDMT1) in T cells and immunotherapy response is peripheral to the group's core areas of AI pathology, tumor heterogeneity, drug resistance mechanisms, and patient-derived models, and the validation is limited to public databases and a small TMA cohort.

articles.title: Advancing Early Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Ki-67 Expression Prediction With Ultrasound Viscoelastography: Based on Peritumoral Assessment.
articles.why_relevant: While the study examines Ki-67 prediction and breast cancer diagnosis, it focuses on ultrasound viscoelastography rather than the group's core areas of histopathology AI, molecular profiling, or patient-derived models, and the validation is modest (single-centre, no independent cohort).

articles.title: QuRad: Radiomics Feature Extraction for QuPath.
articles.why_relevant: QuRad is a QuPath extension for standardized radiomic feature extraction from whole-slide images including breast cancer tissue, which could be a useful tool for the group's digital pathology and image analysis workflows, though it is primarily an infrastructure/tooling paper with limited direct methodological novelty.

articles.title: Breast mammary gland dataset (BMGD): DAPI-stained fluorescent images for nuclei segmentation.
articles.why_relevant: A publicly available annotated nuclei segmentation dataset from breast mammary organoids could support the group's digital image analysis and organoid model work, though it is fluorescence-based (DAPI) rather than H&E and the journal level is low.

articles.title: Integrated Spatial and Bulk Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Multicellular Ecosystem Involved in Progression of Young Breast Cancer.
articles.why_relevant: While the spatial transcriptomics and TME ecosystem analysis are methodologically adjacent to the group's interests, this study focuses on age-defined breast cancer subgroups using mostly public bulk data with limited independent validation, and does not directly address the group's core areas of AI pathology, drug resistance mechanisms, or patient-derived models.

articles.title: Intratumoral Microbiome-Tumor Microenvironment Crosstalk in Breast Cancer Aggressiveness.
articles.why_relevant: While touching on tumor microenvironment and drug resistance themes relevant to the group, this review on intratumoral microbiome in breast cancer is published in a low-impact journal, lacks experimental validation, and is too peripheral to the group's core areas of digital pathology, molecular profiling, and patient-derived models.

articles.title: ACSF2 Functions as a regulatory switch for PARP inhibitor sensitivity in platinum-sensitive and homologous recombination-proficient high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This study addresses PARP inhibitor resistance in ovarian cancer, not breast cancer, and has no meaningful connection to the group's core areas of breast cancer pathology, AI histopathology, or patient-derived breast cancer models.

articles.title: Automated radiosynthesis and biodistribution of [18F]fluoroflutamide.
articles.why_relevant: This paper is about PET radiotracer synthesis for androgen receptor imaging in prostate cancer models and has no meaningful connection to the group's work on breast cancer pathology, digital image analysis, or patient-derived models.

articles.title: Advanced diffusion-weighted imaging for evaluating neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.
articles.why_relevant: This review covers MRI-based imaging for NAC response monitoring in breast cancer, but focuses on radiology techniques rather than histopathology, AI, molecular biomarkers, or patient-derived models central to the group's work.

articles.title: A mechanistic learning framework for breast cancer relapse prediction.
articles.why_relevant: While the paper uses routine histopathological and IHC biomarkers (grade, ER, PR, HER2, lymph nodes) for relapse prediction in METABRIC, it is primarily a mathematical modeling proof-of-concept with only internal cross-validation, modest performance (C-index 0.654), no independent cohort validation, and no direct connection to the group's AI pathology, tumor heterogeneity, or patient-derived model work.
